https://kz.kursiv.media/en/2026-10-19/en.body: Kazakhstan’s health ministry assesses risk of mpox spread as low Published October 19, 2026 11:52 Nikolai Marchenko Senior Journalist n.marchenko@kursiv.media Olesya Bassarova General News Correspondent o.bassarova@kursiv.kz Photo: Unsplash, photo editor: Milosh Muratovskiy Kazakhstan’s Ministry of Healthcare considers the risk of a widespread mpox outbreak in the country to be low but does not rule out imported cases. Health screening and quarantine measures have therefore been strengthened at border checkpoints. «Given the reported cases in several countries around the world ... the possibility of the infection being imported into Kazakhstan cannot be ruled out. The risk of widespread mpox transmission among the population is considered low, taking into account the characteristics of pathogen transmission,» the ministry said in a statement. To prevent the infection from being imported and spreading, Kazakhstan has tightened health screening at its borders. Border checkpoints have been equipped with non-contact thermometers, and medical facilities and laboratories are ready to detect the disease. Procedures are also in place to ensure coordination between agencies if a particularly dangerous infectious disease is suspected. These measures are being implemented under a directive issued by Kazakhstan’s Chief State Sanitary Doctor. According to the ministry, health screening across all modes of transport has so far found no travelers suspected of having mpox. Mpox is a viral infection that spreads through close physical contact with an infected person, including contact with rashes and bodily fluids. The virus can also spread through contaminated clothing, bedding and other items, as well as through contact with infected animals. The main symptoms of mpox include fever, headache, muscle aches, swollen lymph nodes and a skin rash. As a preventive measure, the Ministry of Healthcare recommends avoiding close contact with people who have unexplained skin rashes or other signs of infection. If symptoms of mpox appear, especially after travel to countries where cases have been reported, medical advice should be sought and the doctor informed about the trip and any possible contact with infected people. Previous reports said that five people suspected of having mpox had been hospitalized in Russia. Share Link copied

https://en.kabar.kg/news/state-auditing-.body: Kabar Agency Bishkek, Oct. 19, 2026. /Kabar/. The consolidated budget of Kyrgyzstan has surpassed 1 trillion soms, which has increased the responsibility for the use of state funds; therefore, every som of the budget must serve the people. This was stated in a congratulatory message from President Sadyr Zhaparov to the participants of an event marking the 30th anniversary of the establishment of the Chamber of Accounts. The head of state noted that the history of the Chamber of Accounts is closely linked to the country’s development path throughout its years of independence, and emphasized that the Constitutional Law adopted on May 31, 2023, marked the beginning of a new stage in the development of state auditing. "Today, the Chamber of Accounts is an institution that conducts state audits and holds a special place in ensuring state financial discipline," the message says. The president highlighted that, given the expansion of the state budget’s capacity and the implementation of major infrastructure and social projects across the country, the effective use of state funds takes on particular importance. "We must not only verify where budget funds are directed, but also clearly see what results they have delivered for the state and the people. Audit findings should be measured by concrete changes in public administration, and the recommendations provided must be implemented in practice," Sadyr Zhaparov emphasized. He also noted the necessity of maintaining the independence of the Chamber of Accounts, as well as the objectivity and professional integrity of its auditors. According to the head of state, the introduction of digital mechanisms has enhanced the transparency of financial and economic operations and created new opportunities for identifying shadow economic activity. Electronic waybills and electronic invoices help facilitate the work of state audit authorities. "We must reach a new level in the work of state auditing. Activities should be aimed not only at addressing the consequences of offenses that have already occurred but also at developing the capacity to prevent them," the president stated in his congratulatory message. Furthermore, Sadyr Zhaparov noted that the Chamber of Accounts should become an institution that identifies risks in advance and contributes to improving the quality of public administration. He added that cooperation and the exchange of experience with international supreme audit institutions are also important. The president expressed his gratitude to veterans for their contributions to strengthening state financial discipline and developing the country, and he wished the staff of the Chamber of Accounts success in their vital and responsible work. It should be noted that the president’s congratulatory address was read out by Adylbek Kasymaliev, Chairman of the Cabinet of Ministers. Print

https://24.kg/article/batma-zholboldueva.body: Активистка Батма Жолболдуева отправилась пешком из Баткенской области в Бишкек, добиваясь решения своего вопроса. Несмотря на встречу с представителями областной администрации, она отказалась прекращать путь. Об этом сообщила пресс-служба полномочного представителя президента в Баткенской области. По данным ведомства, 18 октября, после появления информации о пешем походе Жолболдуевой, полпред президента Мамыржан Рахимов поручил разобраться в ситуации, разъяснить активистке законные способы решения ее проблемы и принять во внимание ее безопасность. Первый заместитель полпреда Бактыбек Токсонбаев встретился с Жолболдуевой в селе Жаны-Жер Баткенского района. Во время разговора ей объяснили порядок рассмотрения обращения, однако она не согласилась с предложенным вариантом и продолжила путь в Бишкек. В областной администрации также сообщили, что ведут переговоры с администрацией президента об организации личного приема Батмы Жолболдуевой у Садыра Жапарова. По информации администрации президента, сейчас утверждается план мероприятий по проведению встречи главы государства с жителями Баткенской области. После согласования списка граждан, которые смогут попасть на личный прием, предполагается организовать встречу с участием представителей профильных министерств. Точная дата и время приема пока не определены. В пресс-службе напомнили, что 11 октября Батма Жолболдуева уже обращалась к Садыру Жапарову со своей личной проблемой во время встречи президента с жителями Баткенской области. Власти региона утверждают, что Мамыржан Рахимов ранее неоднократно принимал активистку, однако решение ее вопроса в значительной степени относится к компетенции правоохранительных органов. При этом в официальном сообщении не уточняется, чего именно добивается Батма Жолболдуева. Областная администрация заявила о готовности рассматривать обращения граждан и содействовать решению их проблем в рамках законодательства. Напомним, в декабре 2024 года блогер Батмакан Жолболдуева заявила об изнасиловании ее в ИВС, бездействии правоохранительных, надзорных органов и чиновников. По ее словам, инцидент произошел в апреле 2022-го. Активистка считает, что начальник ИВС отправил к ней насильника из-за произошедших между ними разногласий.

The Speaker of the Azerbaijani Parliament, Sahiba Gafarova, met with the Speaker of the Jogorku Kenesh, Marlen Mamataliev, as part of her visit to the Kyrgyz Republic, and discussed the development of relations between the countries at the level of alliance, the expansion of interparliamentary cooperation, humanitarian ties, and mutual support within international organizations. This was reported by the press service of the Azerbaijani Parliament. Meanwhile, it was noted that during the meeting, the significance of historical, cultural, and national-spiritual ties between the two peoples was emphasized. The parties expressed satisfaction with the high level of relations between the two countries, as well as with the mutual visits, meetings, and contacts that have taken place. They reaffirmed the particular importance of developing fraternal relations between Azerbaijan and Kyrgyzstan. During the talks, it was noted that President Ilham Aliyev’s most recent state visit to the Kyrgyz Republic was a significant event and helped elevate bilateral relations to the level of an alliance. It was emphasized that, thanks to the efforts of the heads of state, ties between the countries are developing rapidly, and cooperation is expanding in many areas. The meeting also highlighted the importance of developing humanitarian ties and initiatives that contribute to further rapprochement between the peoples of the two countries. Marlen Mamataliev noted that the secondary school in the village of Khidirli in the Aghdam district, gifted by the Kyrgyz people, as well as the Heydar Aliyev School and Sports Complex in Bishkek and the Nizami Ganjavi School, are symbols of sincere friendship and brotherhood between the peoples. He noted that they also highly appreciated the erection of a monument to Chingiz Aitmatov in Baku as an expression of attention and respect for the memory of the great Kyrgyz writer. Speaker of the Azerbaijani Parliament Sahiba Gafarova emphasized that the historical, cultural, and spiritual roots uniting the peoples play an important role in the development of bilateral relations. She noted the importance of interparliamentary ties in strengthening these relations. During the meeting, it was noted that relations between the parliaments of the two countries have continued to develop in line with the high level of intergovernmental ties. The importance of expanding the activities of parliamentary committees and friendship groups was emphasized. The parties noted the important role of cooperation within the framework of the Parliamentary Assembly of Turkic States (TURKPA) in expanding interparliamentary ties. They also emphasized the importance of expanding interparliamentary cooperation among Turkic states. During the discussion, the importance of mutual support within international organizations was highlighted. It was emphasized that the countries consistently support one another in these forums, and confidence was expressed that Azerbaijan and Kyrgyzstan will continue to support one another in the future. At the conclusion of the meeting, the parties exchanged views on expanding interparliamentary cooperation and reached a mutual understanding on several issues. Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has appointed Arman Abdrasilov as head of the Situation Center of the Office of the Security Council and Azamat Dyusembekov as head of the Law Enforcement System Department of the Office, according to the presidential administration. Abdrasilov has extensive experience in information technology, cybersecurity, and digital transformation. According to Kazakhstan's Paragraph information system, from 2001 to May 2002, he worked as an engineer at the Institute of Mathematics and Mechanics at Al-Farabi Kazakh National University. From May 2002 to June 2012, he was an engineer at a scientific and technical center. From 2013 to August 2020, he was a co-founder, visionary, and government relations director at the Center for Analysis and Investigation of Cyber Attacks group of companies. In 2018-2019, he worked in compliance at Facebook App in the United States. From August 2020 to October 2022, Abdrasilov served as chairman of the board of the national information and communications holding company Zerde. From November 2022 to February 2025, he was a managing partner at Brain Trust, focusing on capital management and digital transformation consulting. During the same period, he served as a senior adviser on IT development and cybersecurity in Central Asia at Canada's SecDev Foundation. From February to August 2025, he served as deputy head of the Security Council's Department of Current Security Issues. Since August 8, 2025, he has headed the Security Council's Situation Center. Abdrasilov has also held a number of other positions, including membership in the United Nations Economic and Social Commission for Asia and the Pacific (ESCAP) bureau on IT infrastructure development and data management in Central Asia. He worked as an IT and cybersecurity consultant for the Civil Initiative on Internet Policy public foundation in Kyrgyzstan and served on the IT committee of Kazakhstan's National Chamber of Entrepreneurs Atameken. He has also worked as an international consultant on government digitalization in Azerbaijan, Kyrgyzstan and Uzbekistan, and served on the boards of several organizations, including the State Technical Service, National Information Technologies, QazInnovations, Astana Hub and Astana IT University. Abdrasilov has been a member of public councils under several Kazakh ministries and an expert at the Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe (OSCE). Azamat Dyusembekov has extensive experience in Kazakhstan's prosecution system and the Security Council's law enforcement structures. He worked in the prosecution authorities, including as head of a department at the Karaganda Region Prosecutor's Office and in various departmental and service leadership positions at the Prosecutor General's Office of Kazakhstan. From 2018 through 2019, he served as first deputy prosecutor of Aktobe Region. From 2019 through 2022, he was deputy head of the Security Council's Law Enforcement System Department. From August 2022 through September 1, 2023, he headed the Law Enforcement System Department of the Security Council under the Presidential Administration of Kazakhstan. https://www.trend.az/azerbaijan/4236435..body: Home Azerbaijan TABIB placed under Azerbaijan's Ministry of Health - decree Azerbaijan News 19 October 2026 11:27 (UTC +04:00) Photo: Artificial intelligence Aysel Mammadli Editor Read more BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 19. The public legal entity Management Union of Medical Territorial Units (TABIB) has been placed under the authority of Azerbaijan's Ministry of Health. President Ilham Aliyev has signed a decree to this effect. The document was published on the official website of the President of Azerbaijan. Under the decree, the rights, obligations and property of the existing public legal entity will be transferred to TABIB, which will operate under the Ministry of Health. TABIB's authorized capital will be formed from the property of the existing public legal entity. Until TABIB is registered in accordance with the Law of the Republic of Azerbaijan on State Registration and the State Register of Legal Entities, the existing public legal entity will continue operating. During this period, the powers of its Supervisory Board will be exercised by a commission established by the Ministry of Health. TABIB's day-to-day management will be carried out by a Management Board consisting of a chairperson and four deputy chairpersons, all appointed and dismissed by the Ministry of Health. The decree assigns the following founder's powers over TABIB to the President of Azerbaijan: - Approval of TABIB's charter and determination of the amount of its authorized capital, as well as amendments to them; - Establishment of TABIB's governing bodies; - Reorganization and liquidation of TABIB; - Adoption of the decision stipulated in Article 3.3 of the Law on Public Legal Entities. The Ministry of Health is entrusted with resolving other matters falling within the founder's powers under Article 8.2 of the Law on Public Legal Entities, except for those specified in Clause 3.1 of the decree. The Cabinet of Ministers must prepare and submit proposals to the President within three months on the following matters: 1. Improving regulatory legal acts in light of Part 1 of the decree; 2. Drafting TABIB's charter, including the amount of its authorized capital, based on proposals from the Ministry of Health; 3. Resolving other issues arising from the decree. The Ministry of Health is required to establish the commission referred to in Clause 2.3 of the decree. Within three days of approval of TABIB's charter, the ministry must take the necessary steps to register the entity in accordance with the Law on State Registration and the State Register of Legal Entities. Within one month of TABIB's state registration, the ministry must take the necessary measures to transfer the property of the existing public legal entity to TABIB's balance sheet, as appropriate. The ministry must also take any other necessary measures to implement the decree. We are in Baku today to meet with President of Azerbaijan Ilham Aliyev. My name is Yulia Sharifulina and, on behalf of TASS, I will ask the President several questions on the situation around Nagorno-Karabakh. - Hello, Mr. President. - Hello. - Thank you for agreeing to receive us. I understand that you have recently given several interviews to the media but the situation is changing fast and we observe it literally every day. We would like, of course, to dwell more on some basic issues, which, perhaps, are beyond time and which will help our audience to better understand the position of your country. We all witnessed the 11-hour negotiating marathon in Moscow. Do you think it is still possible to return to the fulfillment of the achieved peace or has it failed completely? - We remain true to the commitments within the framework of contacts with our partners. From the very beginning and in the process of negotiations on the settlement of the conflict, we have always relied on international law, on our adherence to the resolution of the conflict by peaceful means, including the commitments Azerbaijan took upon itself after the talks in Moscow, which we aspired to and were going to implement. Unfortunately, Armenia flagrantly violated the ceasefire. Less than 24 hours after the talks, the city of Ganja was attacked. Residential areas of the sleeping city of Ganja were targeted deliberately. After the first attack – and there were two of them – the death toll was very high. In other words, Armenia violated the ceasefire in a defiant manner. Thus, it demonstrated disrespect for mediators, disrespect for the commitments it had assumed after such long negotiations in Moscow. Prior to that, after the terms of the ceasefire for the exchange of bodies, prisoners and hostages had been agreed, Armenia had also violated the ceasefire on the battlefield. However, this seemed insufficient for them and they attacked the city of Ganja. In fact, two days ago, they did the same and again at night. This is a very heinous crime. This is international terrorism. The unanimous condemnation of this bloody crime by the world community means that they will not get away with it. The UN Secretary General, the European Union and many countries at the national level have condemned this act of international terrorism. It is not our fault that the situation is still in the hot phase. I have repeatedly said that Azerbaijan is committed to the principles of settlement. These principles have been developed over the many years of negotiations. I have confirmed in my speeches and in recent contacts with the media that if Armenia acts constructively in the process of negotiations, we are ready to suspend military operations as early as tomorrow. However, the statements we have been hearing from Yerevan completely contradict the fundamental principles developed by the OSCE Minsk Group. The Armenian leadership has recently made very dangerous statements that effectively refute the fundamental principles. In principle, all the activities of Armenia’s new leadership are aimed at disrupting the process of negotiations. Not to undermine this process, but to disrupt it. I have already talked about their numerous statements, provocative actions and attacks on Azerbaijan’s civilian population. Therefore, if the Armenian side finally realizes that the path of military provocations leads them to disaster, we are ready to suspend military operations and resolve the issue at the negotiating table. - Would your country agree to the need for an urgent military meeting, as Russia says? If so, what format and with the participation of what parties could this meeting be held? - You know, the political will of the leadership of Armenia and Azerbaijan is paramount here. There is political will on our side. I confirm our position again today. And I confirm it when we have announced the liberation of 13 more settlements in the occupied territories, when the Armenian army is essentially suffering a defeat, when Azerbaijan demonstrates its advantage on the battleground. Nevertheless, not wishing to continue the bloodshed and wishing to save people’s lives, we are ready to resolve this issue by political means. With regard to military-to-military contacts, the fundamental principles explicitly define this, and we are committed to the fundamental principles I have already mentioned. I think there is no point in repeating – it is the return of the territories occupied by the Armenian side, negotiations on the future of Nagorno-Karabakh, the return of refugees and internally displaced persons to their places of origin, including Nagorno-Karabakh, Shusha. All of this is written in fundamental principles, and the Armenian side agreed to all of this at different stages. Therefore, the question you have just asked is covered in the fundamental principles at the end of the agreement – when all the issues related to de-occupation have been settled, the presence of foreign peacekeeping forces is envisaged. But since the key issues requiring settlement were not agreed on, the parties did not approach this issue. Therefore, there was no clear understanding of who these forces would consist of, what international organizations and what countries would be represented there. Therefore, all this has not been discussed. One thing was clear: the composition and location of these peacekeeping forces should be agreed upon by Azerbaijan and Armenia. This has not been defined either. Therefore, there is no line of contact today, the status quo has been removed, we removed it ourselves and did it within the framework of statements by the presidents of Russia, the United States and France, the repeated statements by the heads of state that the status quo was unacceptable. We were hearing these statements but did not see their implementation. Therefore, we implemented it ourselves. So there is no status quo and there is no line of contact. How can some military observers be deployed there technically and where exactly can they be deployed? After all, the situation on the battlefield changes every day. So there will be some foreign observers but where will they stand – on mountains, in valleys, on bridges? So all this requires a very detailed study. This is also a huge risk for those who deem it necessary to send their military contingent there. So all this must be agreed upon: composition, mandate, timing, goals. Of course, all of this should be done within the framework of the fundamental principles, which, as I said, are accepted by us and rejected by the Armenian side. - But if the situation does require it, will your country agree to the introduction of Russian military observers? And if not Russian, what other countries could take part in this mission and what countries would you strongly object to? - You know, Russia, like the United States and France, is a co-chair of the OSCE Minsk Group, and within the framework of this mandate, the countries have very close interaction with each other. During the hot phase of the conflict, I observe both in the Western and Russian media that the Nagorno-Karabakh issue is probably the only issue where there are no disagreements between these countries. And perhaps this is actually the case. Wherever we look, there are sanctions, confrontations, claims, etc., and they are also mutual. Therefore, of course, I am sure that this issue should be agreed upon within the framework of the co-chairmanship format among these countries and, after it is agreed upon, it should be presented to the parties. https://www.azernews.az/region/265790.ht.body: Macron vows crackdown as France erupts in cost-of-living protests 19 October 2026 08:00 (UTC+04:00) AzerNEWS Staff Read more French President condemns “unbridled” violence after nearly 2,400 arrests, hundreds of police injuries and widespread looting French President Emmanuel Macron has vowed to strengthen security and hold those responsible for violence accountable after cost-of-living protests swept across the country, leaving nearly 2,400 people arrested and almost 1,000 police officers and gendarmes injured, according to the interior ministry. Speaking in a televised address to the nation on Sunday, Macron condemned what he described as “unbridled” violence, while acknowledging that protesters had legitimate grievances over the rising cost of living and the prospects facing young people. “Tonight, we all feel anger and shame,” he said, drawing a distinction between demonstrators with legitimate demands and those who had engaged in destruction, vandalism and looting. “Those who have destroyed must pay,” Macron declared, vowing that the government would take an uncompromising stance towards those responsible for the unrest. The interior ministry said almost 1,000 members of the police and gendarmerie had been injured, seven of them seriously, during Saturday's clashes. The violence was described as among the worst episodes of urban unrest France had experienced in years. Fresh clashes in Paris and Lyon Tensions remained high on Sunday, with police deploying tear gas and stun grenades against hundreds of people gathered in a Paris square following calls on social media for an unauthorised demonstration, AFP journalists reported. Some demonstrators threw bottles and rocks at officers, while police made several arrests. Shops were also looted around Place de la République, prompting the deployment of specialist riot police for a second consecutive day. Violence also broke out in the south-eastern city of Lyon, where police intervened to prevent young people from smashing the windows of a luxury clothing store. The unrest caused extensive damage elsewhere. In Limoges, a fire destroyed the city's 19th-century town hall. Local prefect Maurice Barate told French broadcaster LCI that the blaze had been deliberately started. In Lyon, a tourist office in the city centre was also set ablaze amid clashes and looting. The violence had serious consequences for young people caught up in the unrest. A 17-year-old boy lost his right hand after a crowd-control grenade exploded in Saint-Étienne, while a 17-year-old girl lost an eye in Mulhouse, according to prosecutors. Macron faces pressure over police response Macron pledged to increase security and work with local mayors to protect public buildings, businesses and urban centres. He also promised support for businesses affected by the destruction. However, the president stopped short of announcing exceptional measures such as a state of emergency or a curfew. He promised full transparency over the security forces' response, following criticism that preparations for the demonstrations had been inadequate. Macron said he had asked Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez to draw “all necessary lessons”, particularly regarding intelligence gathering and the authorities' ability to anticipate violence. He said he expected clear answers. Opposition politicians have called for the interior minister to be dismissed, adding to the political pressure on the government. Political divisions deepen The unrest has intensified political tensions ahead of France's presidential election, with Macron constitutionally barred from seeking another consecutive term and far-right National Rally leader Marine Le Pen positioning herself as a leading challenger. Le Pen said the crisis showed that Macron's administration was “running on fumes, exhausted and disoriented”. Jordan Bardella, her party's president, dismissed Macron's address as “lamentable”, arguing that the authorities had nothing more to offer the country. Jean-Luc Mélenchon, leader of the left-wing France Unbowed party and another presidential contender, urged the government to address protesters' demands, saying young people needed the crisis to reach a positive conclusion. The demonstrations brought together trade unions, members of the Yellow Vests movement and school students, uniting groups angered by the cost of living and the limited prospects facing younger generations. The unrest has also attracted international attention. US President Donald Trump blamed immigration for the violence, writing on social media that France was burning and claiming that immigration had shattered the country. His remarks added an international political dimension to a crisis rooted in domestic economic and social tensions. Macron, meanwhile, called for the presidential election campaign to be conducted through political debate rather than street violence, saying France deserved a proper electoral contest. For the French government, the immediate challenge is to restore order while addressing public anger over living costs and opportunities for young people. The scale of the destruction, the injuries sustained by security personnel and the criticism of the police response have left Macron facing mounting pressure to demonstrate that his administration can regain control of the situation. Listen to this article 8 min This audio is automated Learn more Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Russian strikes overnight targeted power substations in multiple regions, leaving tens of thousands of households without electricity, as Ukrainian and Russian officials reported civilian deaths following overnight drone attacks on October 18. Zelenskyy said Russia had carried out 76 attacks on Ukraine's energy and oil and gas sectors in the week since US President Donald Trump announced an energy cease-fire. Trump said on October 11 that he had asked Russian President Vladimir Putin to observe a weeklong pause in attacks on energy infrastructure amid freezing weather in Ukraine. "Over the past week, Russia launched nearly 2,700 attack drones, 1,700 guided aerial bombs, and 66 missiles at Ukraine, most of them ballistic missiles," Zelenskyy wrote on social media on October 18. Accusing Moscow of seeking to plunge Ukraine into a nationwide blackout, Zelenskyy wrote on social media: "Russia is not taking steps toward peace." Zelenskyy said that power stations were targeted in the Vinnytsya, Zhytomyr, Khmelnytskiy, and Odesa regions in the overnight strikes. SEE ALSO: The Coming Cruel Winter: Ukrainians Brace For The Worst Amid Russia's Escalating Air Campaign Russian attacks killed at least two people and injured several others in Ukraine, Ukrainian officials said. In the southeastern city of Zaporizhzhya, a 27-year-old woman was killed and two people were injured, including a six-year-old girl, according to the regional military administration . The attacks damaged two apartment buildings, 18 cars, and an educational institution, the administration said. In the central city of Poltava, a Russian drone attack killed one woman and injured four other people, the head of the city's military administration, Vitaliy Dyakivnych, said on Telegram. Nine residential buildings were damaged, some by falling drone debris. In the western Vinnytsia region, Russian drone attacks on critical infrastructure caused power outages, the regional military administration said. Ukraine's Air Force said Russia had launched 180 combat drones during the overnight attacks, of which 152 were intercepted. Impacts were recorded at 20 locations, it said. Embed share Russia Pounds Ukraine With Missiles And Hundreds Of Drones by RFE/RL Embed share The code has been copied to your clipboard. width px height px The URL has been copied to your clipboard No media source currently available 0:00 0:01:11 0:00 Russia Reports Casualties, Infrastructure Damage In Russia, one person was killed and five injured in a Ukrainian drone attack on St. Petersburg, the city's governor, Aleksandr Beglov, said on October 18. Fires broke out at the St. Petersburg oil terminal, an oil depot, and industrial warehouses, Beglov said. Twelve apartment buildings were also damaged. Russian e-commerce company Ozon said a drone struck one of its logistics facilities in St. Petersburg, causing a fire. Employees were evacuated, and no one was injured at the facility, the company said. The VK Internet company said its data center in the Leningrad region had also been targeted by drones, but its services remained available to users as normal. SEE ALSO: How Ukraine's Strikes On Data Centers Disrupted Taxis, Shopping, And Business In Russia And Beyond A drone struck a cable-stayed bridge forming part of St. Petersburg's Western High-Speed Diameter highway. The extent of the damage was not immediately clear. The attacks also caused power disruptions in parts of the region. Two transformer substations in Yanino were reportedly disconnected, while operations at St. Petersburg's Pulkovo Airport were disrupted. Russia's Defense Ministry said air defense units had downed 1,015 Ukrainian drones over Russian regions overnight. The figure could not be independently verified. Drone attacks also disrupted air travel across Russia. More than 350 flights were delayed or canceled at Moscow's four airports overnight on October 17, as authorities imposed restrictions amid reported Ukrainian drone attacks on the Moscow region. The figures were based on airport departure and arrival boards reviewed by the independent Russian outlet Meduza . Sheremetyevo was the worst affected, with 143 flights canceled and 53 delayed. Vnukovo recorded 55 cancellations and 113 delays, while Domodedovo reported 59 delayed flights. Some flights bound for Moscow were diverted to other cities, including St. Petersburg and Nizhny Novgorod. Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said Russian air defenses had destroyed 75 drones heading toward the capital. Russia's Defense Ministry said more than 600 drones had been destroyed or intercepted across the country overnight, Interfax reported. Airports in Penza, Saratov, and Sochi also suspended operations. Kyiv Says Starshield Connections Still Limited The latest barrage on Ukraine came as disruptions to the Starshield satellite system, the military-grade version of the Starlink service run by Elon Musk's SpaceX, left Ukraine particularly vulnerable earlier in the week. On October 17, Kyiv said the speed of Starshield connections across Ukrainian territory remained significantly limited, causing instability in battlefield communications, medium-range strikes, and the operation of interceptor drones. "The shortage of air defense systems, combined with the lack of confirmation that Starshield's full operational capabilities have been restored, creates additional challenges for Ukraine in protecting critical infrastructure against Russian aerial attacks," Denys Sienik, Ukraine's charge d'affaires to the United States, told RFE/RL. "With colder weather approaching and winter drawing nearer, we fully understand the deliberate nature of Russia's strategy: to systematically damage Ukraine's energy infrastructure and leave civilians without essential services," he added. On October 17, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio rejected claims that the United States had deliberately restricted Ukraine’s access to Starlink, the satellite Internet service operated by Elon Musk’s SpaceX. "No one at the White House ordered anyone to slow down Internet or slow down speed so that certain drones couldn’t use it," he told reporters on October 17 as he prepared to depart for Central Asia, calling reports of US involvement "categorically false." Rubio said his understanding was that Starlink's performance had returned to its previous level. Ukraine had used the commercial service to support drone operations. He also questioned the Ukrainian president's account of the incident, saying he was "not sure Zelenskyy knows what he's talking about." Rubio distinguished Starlink from Starshield, a separate defense-oriented satellite system used by the US military. Ukraine does not currently have access to Starshield, he said, although Kyiv has requested it to conduct deep strikes inside Russia. The question of how the system might be used remains under discussion, Rubio added. His comments highlighted the limits of Ukraine's access to US-linked military technology as tensions between Washington and Kyiv grow over the administration's approach to Russia. https://www.rferl.org/a/belarus-kgb-nati.body: Belarus Exclusive: KGB Complex Rises On Historic Catholic Cemetery Grounds In Minsk By RFE/RL's Belarus Service October 18, 2026 09:00 CET Exclusive: KGB Complex Rises On Historic Catholic Cemetery Grounds In Minsk Share Copy link Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Email Share Share Copy link Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Email Share Prefer us on Google A site plan shows the plot allocated to the National Security Academy in Minsk. The Church of St. Roch is marked in green, the academy building in orange, and the area designated for construction work -- including the laying of utility lines --in pink. Paval Khadzinski has been going to the Church of St. Roch for as long as he can remember, and an ancestor who lived in the 19th century was buried at the Catholic cemetery next to the sanctuary in a central Minsk neighborhood called Zalataya Horka, or Golden Hill. Khadzinski, 41, remembers a time when a playground opened near the church and parishioners hoped a garden would be next: a pleasant green space in the middle of the city. Now, there's a construction site covering a large part of the cemetery, which remained intact despite portions being developed or destroyed during the Soviet era. The government of authoritarian leader Aleksandr Lukashenko has been highly secretive about the site; by the summer of 2025, a massive construction pit was visible in satellite images, and a building frame was standing by February 2026. In some official documents, it is tersely identified as a "multifunctional building," and in others it doesn't exist. By obtaining design documentation and speaking with several people connected to the project, RFE/RL's Belarus Service has learned that the state has chosen the site for a sprawling National Security Academy complex for the KGB -- as the oppressive main security agency is still known -- on the grounds of the former Zalataya Horka cemetery. Moreover, RFE/RL has found that the project is being built based on a decree apparently issued in secret by Lukashenko, allowing builders to bypass an array of legal protections that remain on the books and are designed to preserve such sites. The building under construction adjacent to the Church of St. Roch The construction comes as pressure on the Catholic Church persists despite signs of warming in long-tense ties between predominantly Catholic Poland and mostly Orthodox Christian Belarus: Since the start of this year, at least 20 Polish Catholic priests have been banned from serving or forced to leave the country. Many Polish priests came to Belarus to help rebuild Catholic parish life after decades of Soviet repression, and some have served local communities for decades. "We have a presidential decree," Yuliya Serada, the development project's chief engineer, said when asked what enabled it to go ahead despite the protective legislation. Responding to further questions, Sereda said there had been no change in the protected status of the site, suggesting the decree allowed exemptions for this project. She said the engineers had not planned the archaeological works that are normally required and did know how excavated soil was being handled during construction. 'It's Just Wrong' Independent architects and government opponents said the project put the state's selective attitude toward the rule of law on display in Belarus, where Lukashenko has persistently clamped down on basic freedoms and used fraud-marred votes to extend his rule over the nation of roughly 9 million since he was first elected in 1994. Yuliya Serada receives a commendation from the head of the Belarusian Orthodox Church in 2025. "They didn't even try to pretend they were implementing the law," a Belarusian architect and restorer who works in heritage protection said, speaking on condition of anonymity for security reasons. "Most likely, they immediately went to Lukashenko and said: 'We want to build here, but the law prevents it.' And he says: 'No problem, here's your order, go ahead, go build,'" he told RFE/RL. A law adopted in 2001 prohibits capital construction, with the exception of memorial and religious projects, on the site of old burials. The site's protection-zone plan, approved by the Culture Ministry in 2018, also prohibits the installation of utility networks on the former cemetery grounds. Rights activist and Nobel Peace Prize laureate Ales Byalyatski "A cemetery is a cemetery. No one was going to build anything there," veteran Belarusian human rights activist and 2022 Nobel Peace Prize laureate Ales Byalyatski told RFE/RL. Byalyatski, who spent years in prison before his release under a US-Belarus agreement last December, recalls from his time on the Minsk city council's culture committee in the 1990s that the former cemetery was considered off-limits for development despite being a prime piece of land in a central location. Building a KGB training center on the site "seems very cynical," he said, pointing to the Soviet security services' persecution of the Catholic Church and the continuing pressure on it today. "It's just wrong." The Church of St. Roch and surrounding area, pictured in 2018 The dominant Belarusian Orthodox Church is affiliated with the Moscow-based Russian Orthodox Church and closely tied to the state. Issues concerning historical and cultural heritage sites in Belarus are among those considered by the Republican Council for Historical Policy, which is attached to Lukashenko's administration. 'A Great Joy' The first deputy head of the National Security Academy, Henadz Krasko, is a member of the council. Krasko did not respond to phone calls seeking comment, and the National Security Academy could not be reached for comment. A plan proposed by the parish in 2019 for the space next to the church In the summer of 2018, a small park with a children's playground opened adjacent to the church, with priests and parishioners involved in creating the space and keeping it tidy. That October, the former cemetery was included in a protection zone, approved by the Culture Ministry, where construction and the laying of underground infrastructure were prohibited. "This is a guarantee that the area...will not be built up. It has come under state protection," St. Roch priest Yury Sanko told Vatican News in 2019. "It is a great joy that the Zalataya Horka cemetery, which was not completely destroyed during the Soviet era, will be preserved." Not for long. The state investment program for 2024, approved by Lukashenko, included a clause allocating money for design and survey work for "the construction of a multifunctional building at 5 and 5a Zalataya Horka Street in Minsk" -- a substantial part of the former cemetery grounds. A Planet Labs satellite image of Zalataya Horka, with the protected area shaded in red, the construction site outlined in white, and the Church of St. Roch outlined in green The program said nothing about the purpose of the building, and the government has not disclosed it publicly to this day. In February-March of this year, the district administration held public discussion of changes to the development plan for the Golden Hill area. But the documentation shown to residents provided for a small square on the territory of the former cemetery; there was not a word about the complex that had already been under construction for months. Weapons Storage BelPol, an association of former Belarusian security services officers, reported in 2023 that a new National Security Academy building could be constructed on the cemetery site, with a dormitory designed to house 150 students. The planning documentation obtained by RFE/RL shows that the site has been allocated to the National Security Academy, which is subordinate to the KGB. In a detailed blueprint, the academy building dwarfs the adjacent church, and the footprint of the new structure is made even larger by a surrounding area designated for pipes, power lines, and other infrastructure. https://www.rferl.org/a/kasparov-says-ta.body: Russia Kasparov Says Talks With Putin Pointless, War Is 'Ideological Basis' Of His Rule By Mumin Shakirov October 17, 2026 16:02 CET Kasparov Says Talks With Putin Pointless, War Is 'Ideological Basis' Of His Rule Share Copy link Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Email Share Share Copy link Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Email Share Prefer us on Google Former world chess champion Garry Kasparov speaks to RFE/RL's Mumin Shakirov in Warsaw on October 11. Former world chess champion Garry Kasparov has said ongoing efforts to engage in peace talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin are meaningless because the Kremlin leader has no intention of stopping his nearly five-year war on Ukraine . Speaking in an interview with RFE/RL's Russian Service, Kasparov said international efforts should focus on helping Ukraine achieve victory, adding that this could lead to Putin's fall and a new chance for democracy in Russia. "It's one thing if talks have a chance of solving a problem, with mutual concessions. Putin's plans have not changed. He set himself the goal of liquidating Ukraine as an independent country, and he has not abandoned it," Kasparov said. Fighting For Ukraine After retiring from chess, Kasparov became a prominent opposition figure in Russia before heading into exile in 2013 . Based in the United States, he is now head of the Free Russia Forum, which he founded in 2016. Kasparov has said he was recently warned by US authorities of a Kremlin plot to assassinate him. SEE ALSO: Who’s Who In The Fractured Russian Opposition Fighting Against Putin Speaking to RFE/RL in Warsaw on October 11, Kasparov said exiled Russian political forces should be entirely focused on helping Ukraine win the war. To this end, his own organization had raised some $15 million for various projects in Ukraine. "We are in direct contact with the Free Russia Legion and the RDK ( Russian Volunteer Corps )," he said, referring to two Russian armed groups that have fought on Ukraine's side. "We do fundraising for this." Kasparov also highlighted his work to lobby for Ukrainian causes in Congress, saying that on one occasion his group had persuaded 15 Republicans to switch their votes. This could not be independently confirmed. As well as opposing Putin, the former grandmaster is also known for his longstanding criticism of US President Donald Trump, including Trump's efforts for closer relations with Putin. Kasparov was scathing about Trump's recently announced deal to purchase diesel from Russia . "He continues to work in Putin's interests. His recent comments are the most brazen violation of American laws, including sanction legislation which Trump himself signed," Kasparov said. "His effort to pressure Ukraine seems to me connected to his desperate position three weeks before the (midterm) elections." Trump has said the deal to purchase Russian diesel will provide relief on US and international markets, where diesel shortages caused by the conflict with Iran and exacerbated by Ukrainian attacks on Russian oil refineries have led to price spikes. "Lower prices for Americans, especially our great farmers, ranchers, and truckers, is my greatest priority," Trump posted on social media on October 9. SEE ALSO: Interview: Russia's Shadow War On NATO Is 'Bound To Intensify' The diesel deal has encountered opposition from both sides of the aisle in Congress. Democrats and former officials have also pointed to the Ending Importation of Russian Oil Act of 2022, which prohibits Russian oil imports into the United States unless the president certifies that Russia has met specified conditions, including withdrawing from Ukraine, recognizing Ukrainian sovereignty, and posing no threat to NATO. Plotting Putin's Downfall Kasparov added his voice to a chorus of concern recently from senior officials in European NATO nations that Russia may be preparing some form of escalated aggression toward the alliance, amid what is widely regarded as an ongoing hybrid or shadow campaign that includes drone incursions, sabotage, and assassination attempts. The Kremlin has consistently denied involvement in incidents blamed on it by Western officials. Kasparov also said Putin was completely committed to continuing the war with Ukraine, describing it as "the ideological basis of Putin's rule" visible in the scale of the Russian military budget and in its official propaganda. "Either Ukraine will break under the attacks on its civilian population or it will endure, and then the [Russian] regime will collapse," he said. "This doesn't mean everything will be fine in Russia tomorrow. But the collapse of a regime always means a window of opportunity." Kasparov went on to say that the war had provided "fresh blood" to Putin's power structure, pointing for example to the recent influx of war veterans to the State Duma, the lower house of the Russian parliament. Hundreds or thousands of others could be in other branches of the state hierarchy, he said. However, opinion polls this year have shown falling approval ratings for Putin as the war drags on amid a mounting death toll and increased Ukrainian attacks on refineries, warehouses, and data centers that have affected everyday life in Russia. Kasparov said defeat in Ukraine would fundamentally change the atmosphere in Russian society. "I even believe the overwhelming majority (of Russians) could be prepared to accept democracy and the rule of law," Kasparov said. "It seems to me that failure in war will inevitably force people to think about better alternatives." https://www.rferl.org/a/russia-ukraine-c.body: News Russia's Deadly Attacks Damage Homes, Energy Sites In Ukraine As Kyiv Says Starlink Restrictions Continue By RFE/RL October 17, 2026 12:27 CET Updated October 17, 2026 20:50 CET Russia's Deadly Attacks Damage Homes, Energy Sites In Ukraine As Kyiv Says Starlink Restrictions Continue Share Copy link Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Email Share Share Copy link Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Email Share Prefer us on Google In Slovyansk, in the eastern Donetsk region, Russian forces struck a residential neighborhood with FAB-250 aerial bombs in the early hours of the morning, hitting two apartment buildings, according to local authorities. Russia continued to pound Ukraine with missiles and drones, killing civilians and damaging residential buildings and energy sites, as Kyiv described disruptions to the satellite communications of US company SpaceX, crucial to the country's defense, as a deliberate "operation." Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy called the October 17 barrage "one of [Russia's] largest attacks on Ukraine's energy sector," adding that more than 15 "critical power generation and transmission facilities" were targeted across the country. The worst-hit areas included Lutsk, Rivne, Zhytomyr, Vinnytsya, Shepetivka, Slavuta, and Netishyn, he wrote on X. "Energy facilities in the Kharkiv, Kyiv, Dnipro, and other regions were also hit." SEE ALSO: Trump Waives Graham Act Sanctions On Russia Before They Take Effect According to Ukraine's air force, Russia launched four Kalibr cruise missiles and 332 attack drones, including 31 jet-powered drones, as well as Iskander-M/KN-23 ballistic missiles and Kh-22/32 cruise missiles, over the preceding 24 hours. "The Russians have scaled up their anti-energy operation and are trying to stretch our reserves and repair capabilities as thin as possible," Zelenskyy added. During previous wartime winters, Russia had increasingly targeted Ukraine's energy and civilian infrastructure, leaving thousands without heat or electricity amid freezing temperatures in an effort to force Kyiv into accepting its hard-line demands to end the long-running war. Despite last week's announcement of an energy cease-fire between Ukraine and Russia by US President Donald Trump, who made ending Russia's war on Ukraine a priority when he began his current term in January 2025, Moscow has shown no intention of changing its tactics. On October 16, speaking at what Russian media said was a command post, Russian President Vladimir Putin ordered the country's forces to continue their "massive and coordinated strikes against enemy targets." Embed share Russia Pounds Ukraine With Missiles And Hundreds Of Drones by RFE/RL Embed share The code has been copied to your clipboard. width px height px The URL has been copied to your clipboard No media source currently available 0:00 0:01:11 0:00 A day after Putin's latest order to the Russian military, a Russian air strike in the Korabelnyi district of Ukraine's southern city of Kherson killed a 64-year-old emergency medical services driver, regional military administration head Yaroslav Shanko said. In Slovyansk, in the eastern Donetsk region, Russian forces struck a residential neighborhood with FAB-250 aerial bombs in the early hours of the morning, hitting two apartment buildings, according to local authorities. One person was killed and 10 others were wounded in the attack, four of whom were hospitalized. Eight apartment buildings were damaged, two of them partially destroyed. A total of 16 people were wounded in Slovyansk over the past 24 hours, including a 17-year-old girl. Vehicles and municipal equipment were also damaged. The strikes also placed further strain on Ukraine's electricity system. National grid operator Ukrenergo announced emergency power cuts in several regions, saying that previously published outage schedules would not apply in areas affected by the measures. Energy workers were working to restore supplies, and authorities urged consumers who still had electricity to use it sparingly. In Vinnytsya, the regional capital in central Ukraine, Russian attacks left the city without electricity, Mayor Serhiy Morhunov said. Officials were assessing the extent of the damage, while critical infrastructure switched to backup power. SEE ALSO: Russia Still Needs More Soldiers. The Kremlin Is Still Desperate To Avoid Mobilization The latest barrage came as disruptions to the Starshield satellite system, the military-grade version of the Starlink service run by Elon Musk's SpaceX, left Ukraine particularly vulnerable earlier in the week. On October 17, Kyiv said the speed of Starshield connections across Ukrainian territory remained significantly limited, causing instability in battlefield communications, medium-range strikes, and the operation of interceptor drones. "The shortage of air defense systems, combined with the lack of confirmation that Starshield’s full operational capabilities have been restored, creates additional challenges for Ukraine in protecting critical infrastructure against Russian aerial attacks," Denys Sienik, Ukraine's charge d'affaires to the United States, told RFE/RL. "With colder weather approaching and winter drawing nearer, we fully understand the deliberate nature of Russia's strategy: to systematically damage Ukraine's energy infrastructure and leave civilians without essential services," he added. Earlier in the week, Musk said that any limitations on Ukraine's speed or use of Starshield were decided by the US military and the US president. Trump said on October 16 that he did not think either he or Musk was responsible for Ukraine's lack of Starlink access. In his latest comments to reporters on October 17, Zelenskyy said Kyiv had sent vehicles equipped with Starlink to the European Union "to understand what was happening" and that there were no speed restrictions there. "We have the relevant evidence," he added. Based on this evidence, the Ukrainian president concluded that Starlink speed restrictions applied only within Ukraine, calling it a "planned operation." SpaceX had already once refused a request from Kyiv for access to the system for operations in the Black Sea near Russian-occupied Crimea, as well as other parts of the front line including Kherson and Donetsk. Musk said at the time that the request was refused because the company "would be explicitly complicit in a major act of war and conflict escalation." SEE ALSO: Kasparov Says Talks With Putin Pointless, War Is 'Ideological Basis' Of His Rule Meanwhile, Ukraine's General Staff said on October 17 that Ukrainian forces remained in control of the eastern town of Dobropillia in the Donetsk region, rejecting a claim by Putin a day earlier that Russian forces had captured the town. Kyiv also disputed Moscow's claim that Russian forces had seized more than 1,800 square kilometers of Ukrainian territory and 92 settlements since September 1, Reuters reported. Among other demands for ending its invasion, Russia has repeatedly said Ukraine must hand over the part of the eastern Donetsk region that Moscow's forces have been unable to capture despite years of deadly fighting. Ukraine says this is unacceptable, signaling that it could agree to a cease-fire that would leave the front lines in place as talks get under way. With reporting by Alex Raufoglu and Reuters. https://www.ozodi.org/a/rubio-dar-samarq.body: Осиёи Марказӣ Тиҷорат, сармоягузорӣ, амният. Рубио дар Самарқанд чиро баррасӣ мекунад? Алекс Рауфоғлу 2 соат пеш Тиҷорат, сармоягузорӣ, амният. Рубио дар Самарқанд чиро баррасӣ мекунад? Ба дигарон фиристед Линкро нусхабардорӣ кунед Facebook X (Twitter) Email Ба дигарон фиристед Ба дигарон фиристед Линкро нусхабардорӣ кунед Facebook X (Twitter) Email Ба дигарон фиристед Бидуни филтршикан Ин пайванд (линк) дар минтақаҳое, ки вебсайти мо бастааст, кор мекунад Мо дар Google Марко Рубио, вазири умури хориҷии Амрико. Акс аз моҳи июли 2026 Марко Рубио, котиби давлатӣ ё вазири корҳои хориҷии Амрико, барои мулоқот бо ҳамтоёни худ аз панҷ кишвари Осиёи Марказӣ, аз ҷумла Тоҷикистон, рӯзи 18-уми октябр ба шаҳри Самарқанд меравад . Иёлоти Муттаҳида талош дорад , робитаҳояшро бо минтақае, ки миёни Русия ва Чин ҷой гирифтааст, устувор кунад. Рубио дар посух ба ин суол, ки чаро дар пасманзари чандин буҳрони байнулмилалӣ ба Узбекистон меравад, гуфт, "ҳадафи ин сафар таҳкими робитаҳо аст, на вокуниш ба ягон буҳрони мушаххас." Ӯ афзуд, замони сафар тавре интихоб шудааст, ки барои ҳамаи панҷ раҳбар ва вазирони корҳои хориҷӣ муносиб бошад. Аз ин пеш, рӯзи 16-уми октябр, як мақоми баландпояи Департаменти давлатӣ ё Вазорати корҳои хориҷии Амрико дар суҳбат бо хабарнигорон гуфт, Вашингтон мехоҳад тамосҳои дипломатии сатҳи баландро ба ҳамкориҳои мушаххаси иқтисодӣ ва амниятӣ табдил диҳад. "Иёлоти Муттаҳида муддати бисёр тӯлонӣ ба Ховари Миёна ва Шарқ тамаркуз карда буд ва Осиёи Марказӣ таваҷҷуҳи заруриро дарёфт накард," -- гуфт ӯ. Сафари Марко Рубио ба Узбекистон бо ҳадафи рушди натиҷаҳои қолаб ё чорчӯби дипломатии “C5+1” сурат мегирад. Нишасте, ки Вашингтонро бо Қазоқистон, Қирғизистон, Тоҷикистон, Туркманистон ва Узбекистон пайванд медиҳад ва меҳвари онро иқтисод, ҷалби сармоя ва ҳамкориҳо дар бахши амният ташкил медиҳад. Навор дар Инстаграм: Сафари намояндагони ширкатҳои амрикоӣ ба Узбекистон Ҳайати ҳамроҳи Марко Рубио аз намояндагони ширкатҳои бузурге чун Boeing, Citibank ва Franklin Templeton, ҳамчунин, ширкатҳои фаъол дар бахши маъданҳои нодир ва дигар соҳаҳои стратегӣ иборат аст. Намояндагони Корпоратсияи молиявии рушди байнулмилалии Амрико, Бонки содироту воридоти Иёлоти Муттаҳида, Шӯрои амнияти миллӣ ва Департаменти давлатӣ низ дар гуфтушунидҳое иштирок хоҳанд кард, ки ҳадафашон эҷоди робита миёни доираҳои тиҷоратии Амрико бо шарикони эҳтимолӣ дар саросари Осиёи Марказӣ аст. Мансабдори баландпояи Вазорати умури хориҷии Иёлоти Муттаҳида рӯзи 16-уми октябр гуфт, танҳо Қазоқистону Узбекистон дар як соли гузашта беш аз 30 миллиард доллар сармояи навро ба Иёлоти Муттаҳида ҷалб кардаанд. Ӯ сармоягузориҳоро барои коргарони амрикоӣ фоидаовар ва нишонаи наздиктар шудани робитаҳои иқтисодии Вашингтон бо ин ду кишвар хонд. Вале дар бораи созишномаҳои нави мушаххасе, ки қарор аст дар Самарқанд ҳосил шаванд, ҷузъиёт надод. Самарқанд, маркази таърихии тиҷорӣ дар Роҳи Абрешим, макони асосии сафари Рубио ба Осиёи Марказӣ аст. Мансабдори Вазорати корҳои хориҷии Амрико гуфт, сафар на танҳо мулоқоти дуҷониба ва нишастҳо дар қолаби “C5+1”, балки тамоси мустақими ширкатҳои амрикоиро бо соҳибкорони минтақа ва намояндагони ҳукуматҳо низ дар бар хоҳад гирифт. Инро ҳам бинед: Таҳлили коршиносон Аз сафари Рубио ба Осиёи Марказӣ чӣ интизоранд? Қазоқистон, “Паймони Иброҳим” ва даъват ба G20 Нияти Қазоқистон барои пайвастан ба “Паймони Иброҳим” аз таҳаввулоти дигари муҳиме буд, ки дар нишасти хабарии рӯзи 16-уми октябр таъкид шуд. Мақоми баландпояи Вазорати корҳои хориҷии Амрико бо баёни “мунтазир бошед” санаи дақиқеро барои имзои паймон нагуфт, аммо афзуд, тарафҳо умедворанд, ин равандро “ҳарчи зудтар” ба поён расонанд. “Паймони Иброҳим” дар оғоз барои одӣ кардани равобит миёни Исроил ва чанд кишвари арабӣ таъсис шуда буд. Пайвастани эҳтимолии Қазоқистон доираи ин чаҳорчӯбро васеъ хоҳад кард, ҳарчанд мақоми Департаменти давлатӣ дар бораи шартҳо ё замони пайвастани расмии кишвар ҷузъиёте надод. Ин мақом ҳамчунин гуфт, Қазоқистон ва Узбекистон бори нахуст ба ҳайси нозир ба нишасти Гурӯҳи 20 (G20) даъват шудаанд. Ин даъватҳо ҳамчун бахше аз талошҳои густурдаи Вашингтон барои боло бурдани ҷойгоҳи байнулмилалии Осиёи Марказӣ ва бештар кардани равобит бо ҳукуматҳои минтақа муаррифӣ шуданд. Мансабдори Департаменти давлатӣ ҳамзамон гуфт, раҳбарони панҷ кишвари Осиёи Марказӣ аз Доналд Трамп, раисҷумҳури Амрико, даъват кардаанд, ки ба кишварҳои онҳо сафар кунад ва афзуд, ҳукуматҳои минтақа аз фаъолтар шудани Вашингтон хуб истиқбол кардаанд. ИНЧУНИН, БИХОНЕД: Сенатор Ҷон Куртис: "Субот дар Осиёи Марказӣ барои манфиатҳои ИМА муҳим аст" Мубориза бо терроризм низ ҳаст Тиҷорат ва сармоягузорӣ ягона авлавиятҳо нестанд. Мақоми баландпояи Департаменти давлатӣ гуфт, Иёлоти Муттаҳида ҳамчунин ҳамкориҳоро дар мубориза бо терроризм бо баъзе аз кишварҳои Осиёи Марказӣ тақвият медиҳад. Ин мақом аз ягон кишвар ном набурд ва дар бораи ташаббусҳо ҷузъиёт надод, аммо ҳамкориҳои амниятиро як бахши муҳими равобити рӯ ба густариши Вашингтон бо минтақа хонд. Талошҳои Амрико барои густариши робитаҳо дар ҳолест, ки ҳукуматҳои Осиёи Марказӣ бо Русия ва Чин муносибати худро нигоҳ дошта, ҳамзамон мекӯшанд доираи шарикиҳои байнулмилалии худро васеъ кунанд. Мансабдори Департаменти давлатӣ ин ташаббусро кӯшише барои берун рондани яке аз ин ду қудрат надонист ва баръакс, ба имкониятҳои тиҷоратӣ, тақвияти тамосҳои дипломатӣ ва ҳамкорӣ дар масъалаҳои муштараки амниятӣ таъкид кард. Чаҳорчӯби "C5+1" ба яке аз абзорҳои асосии ҳамкории Иёлоти Муттаҳида бо минтақа табдил шудааст. Ин мақом гуфт, Трамп соли гузашта барои нахустин бор нишасти раҳбарони "C5+1"-ро дар Кохи Сафед мизбонӣ кард, ки дар он раисони ҷумҳури ҳамаи панҷ кишвари Осиёи Марказӣ гирди ҳам омаданд. Пардабардорӣ Пайванд нусхабардорӣ шуд ТАРҲҲО Русский Пайгирӣ кунед Ҳамаи сомонаҳои RFE/RL Ҷустуҷӯ РУС TV TV Ҷустуҷӯ Пешӣ Баъдӣ Хабари нав Дар чанд ҷумла Октябр 18, 2026 "Тиргон"-ро дар Тоҷикистон ҷашни расмӣ эътироф карданд Бинои порлумони Тоҷикистон Вакилони Маҷлиси Намояндагон, палатаи поёнии порлумони Тоҷикистон, иди бостонӣ ё куҳани Тиргон ро, ки замони таҷлилаш ба чиллаи тобистон рост меояд ва бо номи даъвати борон низ машҳур аст, ҷашни миллӣ ва расмӣ эътироф кардаанд. Тасмими онҳо рӯзи 12-уми октябр бо ислоҳи қонуни танзими ҷашну маросим эълон шуд. Бино ба матни ҷаласаи порлумон, ки Радиои Озодӣ 18-уми октябр дид, Шаҳбози Аброр, вакил аз Ҳизби демократ, гуфтааст, лоиҳа ба Қонуни асосӣ мухолифат надорад ва харҷи изофиро аз буҷа талаб намекунад. Шарҳи бештари мақомот дар бораи ҷашни Тиргон ва сабабҳои пазируфтани он дақиқ нест. Пештар намояндагони Академия ё Фарҳангистони миллии илмҳои Тоҷикистон гуфта буданд, ки ҷашни Тиргон "ба манзури ягонагии инсон ва табиат таҷлил мешавад" ва идомаи мантиқии Меҳргону Сада ва Наврӯз аст. "Кишоварзон дар фасли тобистон бо камбуди об рӯ ба рӯ мешаванд ва даъвати борон барои ҳалли ин мушкил аст," -- гуфта буд Фарҳод Раҳимӣ, раиси вақти Фарҳангистони миллии илмҳо. Дар ҳамин ҳол, иқдоми ба ин монанд дар дини Ислом бо номи "намози истисқо" ё талаби борон вуҷуд дорад. Соли 2025 дар пайи хушксолии дароз дар намозҳои рӯзи ҷумъа дар Тоҷикистон ва Узбекистон аз Худо борон талаб карданд . Чанд сол боз дар Тоҷикистон ба ҷуз аз идҳои бостонии Наврӯз, Меҳргон ва Сада, ҷашнҳои дигаре чун иди каду, ангур, картошка ва асалу харбуза низ баргузор мешавад. Мақомот баргузории чунин иду ҷашнҳоро барои рушди ин соҳаҳо муҳим мешуморанд. Мунтақидон мегӯянд, азбаски дар кишвар мушкилот зиёд аст, мақомот мехоҳанд, бо таҷлили чунин ҷашнҳо таваҷҷуҳро ба самти дигар бикашанд. Бархеи дигар мақомотро барои, ба гуфтаи онҳо, харҷҳои беҳуда танқид мекунанд ва пешниҳод доранд, ҳукумат ба ҷойи ингуна маъракаҳо беҳтар ба аст ҷойҳои корӣ биофаранд ва вазъи зиндагии мардумро беҳбуд бахшанд. Изҳороти Сергей Лавров рӯзи 16-уми октябр дар нишасти намояндагони Созмони Паймони Амнияти Дастҷамъӣ, Иттиҳоди Давлатҳои Мустақил ва Созмони Ҳамкориҳои Шонгҳой садо дод. Хабаргузории русии "ТАСС" суханони ӯро чунин иқтибос овардааст: "Мо ин воқеиятро низ ба назар мегирем, ки тибқи маълумоти мавҷуда, дар минтақаҳои Афғонистон дар марз бо Тоҷикистон, Туркманистон ва Узбекистон ҳузури ҷиддии гурӯҳҳои террористӣ ва ифротӣ, урдугоҳҳои омӯзишӣ ва пойгоҳҳои онҳо ҳамоно боқӣ мондааст." Инро ҳам бинед: Изҳори нигаронии як созмони мухолифи ҳукумати Тоҷикистон аз хатари шохаи "Хуросон" Лавров гуфтааст, ҷангҷӯёни гурӯҳҳои террористӣ метавонанд аз хоки Афғонистон бо баҳонаи паноҳандагӣ ё саёҳат кӯшиши ворид шудан ба кишварҳои минтақаро кунанд. Вазири корҳои хориҷии Русия афзудааст, бино ба арзёбии хадамоти вижаи кишвараш, хатари асосӣ аз ҷангҷӯёни "Шохаи Хуросон"-и созмони террористии “Давлати исломӣ” ё ДОИШ бармеояд. Ин дар ҳолест, ки ҳанӯз моҳи феврали имсол Александр Зуев, муовини дабири кулли Созмони Милал д ар нишасти Шӯрои Амният гуфта буд, "Шохаи Хуросон" дар Афғонистон як таҳдиди ҷиддӣ барои минтақа ва фаротар аз он ба шумор меравад. “Толибон”, гурӯҳи ҳоким дар Афғонистон, иддао мекунад, ки "Шохаи Хуросон" саркӯб шуда, дигар наметавонад барои ин кишвар мушкил эҷод кунад. Сергей Шойгу, дабири Шӯрои амнияти Русия, дар нишасти рӯзи 16-уми октябр шумораи намояндагони созмонҳои террористиро дар Афғонистон зиёда аз 23 ҳазор нафар эълон кардааст. Тоҷикистон бо Афғонистон тақрибан 1400 километр марз дорад. Мақомот дар Душанбе пинҳон намекунанд, ки аз ҳузури ҷангҷӯён дар он сӯи Ому нигарон ҳастанд, аммо Кумитаи давлатии амнияти миллӣ дар чанд изҳороти пешинааш гуфтааст, барои таъмини амният дар марз "аз тамоми қувваю восита истифода намуда, ба сарҳадшиканон ҷавоби сазовори қонунӣ хоҳад дод ". Владимир Путин, президенти Русия, рӯзи якуми сентябри 2026 дар мулоқот бо раисҷумҳури Тоҷикистон Эмомалӣ Раҳмон гуфта буд, аз нигарониҳои амниятии Душанбе , бахусус дар мавриди рӯйдодҳои Афғонистон, огоҳ аст, аммо шарҳ надод, ки ишорааш ба чист. Инро ҳам бинед: Путин гуфт, аз нигарониҳои амниятии Тоҷикистон огоҳ аст Шохаи “Хуросон”-и гурӯҳи ба ном “Давлати исломӣ” дар соли 2015 аз вуҷуди худ хабар дод ва дар солҳои охир масъулияти чанд ҳамлаи маргборро дар дохил ва берун аз Афғонистон ба дӯш гирифт. Вазорати корҳои хориҷии Амрико барои маълумоте, ки боис ба боздошти ду раҳбари "Шохаи Хуросон"-и гурӯҳи "Давлати исломӣ" ё ДОИШ шавад, 18 миллион доллар ҷоиза ваъда додааст. Иёлоти Муттаҳида гурӯҳи ДОИШ-ро созмони террористӣ медонад. Аз ҷумла, тибқи омори Вазорати маорифи Русия, дар соли таҳсили 2025-2026 шумораи муҳассилин аз Тоҷикистон, Узбекистон ва Қирғизистон дар ин кишвар 27 дарсад коҳиш ёфт. قدی بالاست که برای عابران و موتورسواران و حتی خودروهای مجاور خطرناک است. ماشین جدید تسلا به همین خاطر مشتریان خاص خود را دارد. خط قرمز رگولاتورها در ایمنی معابر شهری ادارههای ایمنی ترافیک و استانداردهای جادهای قوانین مشخصی برای صدور مجوز شمارهگذاری دارند. این قوانین استفاده از سیستمهای پرتاب مکانیکی یا راکتی را روی خودروهای مجاز خیابانی ممنوع کردهاند. مخازن باد فشرده داخل خودرو برای ثبت تاییدیه تصادف باید آزمایشهای تخریب را پشت سر بگذارند. در تصادفهای رانندگی وجود محفظههای تحت فشار بالا خطر انفجار ثانویه ایجاد میکند. رگولاتورها بدون دریافت نتایج قطعی آزمون ضربه اجازه تردد چنین
