https://www.azernews.az/karabakh/265622..body: Armenia-Azerbaijan peace agreement could be finalized by 2031, Pashinyan says 15 October 2026 13:13 (UTC+04:00) Ulviyya Poladova Read more The peace agreement between Armenia and Azerbaijan should be signed and ratified by 2031, Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan said during a government meeting. Pashinyan noted that he had set this goal for himself and considered it his "personal agenda." "I see this as a possibility; otherwise, I would not have said so," he added. Earlier, Nikol Pashinyan emphasised that Armenia should have a territory of 29,743 square kilometres, while there should be no enclaves or exclaves on either side of the border. According to him, Armenia and Azerbaijan should exchange territories of precisely corresponding sizes. Pashinyan also stressed that all roads and communication routes should remain open. Commenting on his contacts with Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev in Turkmenistan, Pashinyan said he had formed a preliminary impression that the two countries had an opportunity to shape peace along these lines. It should be recalled that on August 8, 2025, following a trilateral meeting in Washington, the leaders of Azerbaijan, Armenia and the United States adopted a Joint Declaration on the peaceful settlement between Baku and Yerevan. Tags: Azerbaijan Armenia Nikol Pashinyan

https://www.azernews.az/business/265597..body: IMF says South Caucasus and Central Asia remain resilient despite Middle East conflict 15 October 2026 11:15 (UTC+04:00) Qabil Ashirov Read more Many countries in the South Caucasus and Central Asia have maintained their economic resilience despite the adverse effects of the ongoing Middle East conflict on global energy markets and trade, International Monetary Fund (IMF) official Jihad Azour has said. The director of the IMF’s Middle East and Central Asia Department made the remarks during a briefing. Azour said economies directly affected by the military conflict were facing significant pressure, while other countries across the Middle East, North Africa, Afghanistan and Pakistan, as well as most states in the South Caucasus and Central Asia, had demonstrated greater resilience. He noted that the region’s economic outlook would depend on the pace of recovery in energy production and international trade, alongside efforts to preserve macroeconomic stability. According to Azour, oil production has fallen sharply in almost all oil-exporting countries directly affected by the conflict. Disruptions to maritime transport and petroleum product supplies have also driven up fuel prices. However, pre-conflict fiscal surpluses, alternative transport routes, oil production outside the Persian Gulf and the use of strategic reserves have helped limit the initial economic losses, keeping them below earlier expectations. The IMF official warned that the capacity of these factors to cushion the economic impact was gradually diminishing. With reserves declining and opportunities to increase production remaining limited, further disruptions to energy supplies could trigger sharper price fluctuations. Azour’s assessment highlights the importance of economic diversification, reliable transport corridors and prudent fiscal policies in helping countries across the South Caucasus and Central Asia withstand external shocks. Tags: Persian Gulf IMF South Caucasus Central Asia North Caucasus

https://www.azernews.az/region/265560.ht.body: Armenia, Russia to establish working group on railway operations 14 October 2026 15:57 (UTC+04:00) Qabil Ashirov Read more Armenia and Russia will establish a joint working group to address issues related to the operation of Armenia’s railway network. The announcement was made in a government statement following a meeting between Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan and Oleg Belozerov, CEO of Russian Railways. “The parties agreed to establish a joint working group within a specified short timeframe to discuss the identified problems, explore possible solutions and clarify the next steps,” the statement said. During the meeting in Yerevan, Pashinyan said the Armenian government aimed to make the country’s railways more competitive and integrate them into the railway networks of neighbouring countries and the wider international network, taking into account opportunities to unblock regional transport infrastructure. In this context, the two sides discussed opportunities arising from regional developments and measures aimed at increasing the competitiveness of Armenia’s railway network and integrating it into international transport routes. “The parties exchanged views on railway reconstruction projects along the Gyumri-Akhurik-Türkiye border and Yeraskh-Nakhchivan (Azerbaijan) sections,” the statement said. The sides also discussed infrastructure development during the concession management period of South Caucasus Railway, the efficiency of the company’s management, existing challenges and possible ways to address them. Tags: Russia Armenia South Caucasus

https://www.azernews.az/nation/265591.ht.body: Azerbaijan, China discuss strategic partnership 15 October 2026 10:00 (UTC+04:00) Qabil Ashirov Read more Azerbaijani Foreign Minister Jeyhun Bayramov has met with Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi during the latter’s working visit to Azerbaijan to attend the seventh Summit of the Conference on Interaction and Confidence Building Measures in Asia (CICA), held under Azerbaijan’s chairmanship. The ministers emphasized that high-level dialogue, mutual trust and friendship between the two peoples remain key driving forces behind bilateral relations. The sides welcomed the rapid development of the Comprehensive Strategic Partnership established in 2025. They noted that the important agreements reached during Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev’s state visit to China had laid a solid foundation for expanding bilateral ties ahead of the 35th anniversary of diplomatic relations between the two countries in 2027. The ministers discussed opportunities to deepen cooperation in trade and economic relations, investment, energy, transport, logistics and connectivity. In this context, they highlighted Azerbaijan’s role as a key link between Asia and Europe and the growing importance of the Middle Corridor in strengthening interregional connectivity. The two sides reaffirmed their commitment to mutual support within the United Nations, CICA and other international platforms. Bayramov and Wang Yi also exchanged views on the broader regional security situation and recent developments, emphasizing the importance of sustained dialogue, diplomatic engagement and multilateral cooperation in addressing existing challenges. Bayramov briefed his Chinese counterpart on the peace process with Armenia, as well as Azerbaijan’s ongoing reconstruction and rehabilitation efforts in territories liberated from occupation during the post-conflict period. Tags: Azerbaijan Ilham Aliyev China Foreign Ministers president Diplomatic relations Middle Corridor

https://www.trend.az/azerbaijan/politics.body: Home Azerbaijan Politics China backs Azerbaijan's CICA chairmanship for another two years – Wang Yi Politics News 15 October 2026 14:21 (UTC +04:00) Photo: Press service of the President of the Republic of Azerbaijan Humay Aghajanova Read more BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 15. Azerbaijan has carried out successful work regarding climate change during its two-year chairmanship of the Conference on Interaction and Confidence Building Measures in Asia (CICA), and therefore China supports Azerbaijan's chairmanship for another two years, Foreign Minister of China, Wang Yi, said at the 7th Summit of CICA in Baku on Thursday, Trend ’s correspondent reports from the event. According to him, CICA is a cooperation platform for the development of Asian countries. He noted that CICA is a platform that supports peace in Asia. "We are currently going through a period of rapid change. We must foster our solidarity so that we can easily overcome crisis situations. The Asian continent is home to the most dynamic and diverse civilizations. We must respect the governance models of each state," he added. The 7th CICA Summit is being held in Baku under Azerbaijan's chairmanship. The meeting will review progress since the launch of CICA's transformation in 2022, as well as the achievements of Azerbaijan's chairmanship in strengthening the organization and advancing practical cooperation among member states. Under the theme “Stronger CICA: Connectivity, Digitalization and Sustainable Growth in Asia,” Azerbaijan has promoted dialogue and results-oriented cooperation during its 2024–2026 chairmanship. https://www.trend.az/azerbaijan/4234763..body: Home Azerbaijan Chronicles of Victory: President Ilham Aliyev interviewed by director general of Russia's media holding on October 15, 2020 (VIDEO) Azerbaijan News 15 October 2026 07:00 (UTC +04:00) BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 15. The Azerbaijani Army launched a counter-offensive operation, later called the "Iron Fist", on September 27, 2020, in response to the large-scale provocation of the Armenian armed forces along the frontline. The 44-day second Karabakh war ended with the liberation of Azerbaijan’s territories from nearly 30-year Armenian occupation and the restoration of territorial integrity. President of the Republic of Azerbaijan Ilham Aliyev has given an interview to Director General of "Rossiya Segodnya International News Agency" media holding Dmitry Kiselev for the Russian RIA Novosti agency. Trend presents the interview. - Mr. President, thank you very much for this opportunity to ask you questions at such a difficult time for Azerbaijan and for the whole world. How would you assess the results of military action since 27 September? What are the losses of the sides, according to your estimates, and are there many prisoners? - On 27 September, Azerbaijan was subjected to yet another attack of the Armenian armed forces. This was not the first attack in the past three months. Something similar but on a smaller scale took place at the state border in July. That attack was repulsed. Then in August, a sabotage group was sent from the Armenian side to commit terrorist acts against the civilian population and against the military and the head of this group was detained and is now giving evidence. At the end of September, our settlements were also subjected to artillery fire, and in the very first hours we had casualties both among the civilian population and among the military. To date, we have 43 civilian deaths and more than 200 wounded, about 2,000 houses in villages and towns adjacent to the line of contact are either completely destroyed or damaged. Unfortunately, artillery shelling from Armenia have continued after the agreement on the parameters of a ceasefire was reached, including the barbaric bombing of the city of Ganja, as a result of which 10 civilians were killed and about 40 were wounded. As for the losses on the battlefield, according to our data, the losses of the Armenian side are much higher than ours. We will announce our losses among servicemen after the active phase of the conflict. As for the results of the military action, they have been very successful for the Azerbaijani army. We have managed to break through the deeply echeloned defenses of the opposing side. In some areas, there were even four lines of defense. The mountainous terrain, of course, makes the defense much easier than the counteroffensive. To date, dozens of settlements have been liberated from the occupation, including the city of Jabrayil and most of the villages of Jabrayil district, the vast majority of villages in Fizuli district, and the settlement of Sugovushan, which is of strategic importance. We have driven the occupiers out of strategic heights on the Murovdag mountain range and continue our successful operation to restore the territorial integrity of our country. - Mr. President, we have been hearing from different sources about the participation of mercenaries from Syria or Libya on the side of the Azerbaijani army. To what extent is this true? - I have already spoken on this topic many times. There is no need for any foreign military participation in Azerbaijan. Our army consists of more than 100,000 fighters and, if necessary, with mobilization, this figure can be increased several times. Today, the armed formations available to us are fully capable of completing any task. Footage of the destruction of Armenian military equipment is available on the Internet. Of course, no mercenary possesses such qualifications and such technical capabilities. We have destroyed more than a billion dollars worth of the opposing side’s military equipment by means of unmanned attack aircraft alone, and this does not include other resources at our disposal. The potential of the Azerbaijani army is well known – what we have is no secret. Therefore, we have no need for additional military forces. Azerbaijan has always been a consistent fighter against international terrorism. We will never allow any terrorist organizations to build nests on our territory, even more so to pose a threat to our people and our neighbors. We will never allow this. No-one has provided us with any evidence of the presence of foreign armed formations on the territory of Azerbaijan in the current clashes. Our official position is that we have no foreign mercenaries. - The Moscow agreements of 10 October mention the fundamental principles of the settlement. Can you please decipher these principles the way you understand them? - These principles have been developed over many years, over more than 10 years, I would say. In the process of my work with the previous leadership of Armenia, we actively moved forward in the process of coordinating positions. It was very difficult. Negotiations are a difficult process in themselves, and even more so on such an important issue. Nevertheless, both sides showed a desire to follow the path of a political settlement. Unfortunately, after the current government of Armenia came to power, everything that had been accumulated before was simply thrown into the waste basket by the Armenian side. https://novastan.org/en/interview/hamed-.body: 14 October 2026 Mathieu Lemoine Tags Afghanistan Politics Spain Afghan President Hamid Karzai greets a delegation upon his arrival in Madrid to attend the International Summit on Democracy, Terrorism and Security, held from 8 to 10 March 2005. His visit preceded the establishment of resident embassies in Madrid and Kabul. Photo: Courtesy of Hamed Wahdat Ahmadzada. Support Novastan, the European Central Asia magazine By supporting Novastan, you are supporting the only English, French and German-language media specialising in Central Asia. We’re independent and we need your help to stay that way! Support Novastan Former Afghan diplomat and political scientist Hamed Wahdat Ahmadzada, who holds a PhD in Political Science from the Autonomous University of Madrid , speaks to Novastan about building Afghanistan’s diplomatic presence in Spain, two decades of international engagement, the collapse of the Afghan Republic, Taliban rule, the Afghan diaspora and what Europe still misunderstands about his country. When Hamed Wahdat Ahmadzada arrived in Madrid in December 2006, Afghanistan did not yet have a resident embassy in Spain. Diplomatic relations between Afghanistan and Spain dated back to 1950, but for decades they had been handled through non-resident embassies. Following the fall of the first Taliban regime and the establishment of Afghanistan’s interim government, the two countries moved towards establishing permanent diplomatic representations in each other’s capitals. Ahmadzada was selected as the first resident Afghan diplomat in Spain because of his previous studies at Madrid’s Diplomatic School, his knowledge of Spanish and his familiarity with the country. He arrived at a moment when Spain was becoming increasingly involved in Afghanistan through diplomacy, its military presence, development cooperation and reconstruction. Almost two decades later, the Afghan Republic Ahmadzada represented no longer exists. The Taliban returned to power in August 2021 after the withdrawal of US and allied forces. Ahmadzada spoke to Novastan Editor-in-Chief Mathieu Lemoine about the relationship he helped build, Spain’s experience in Afghanistan, the achievements and failures of two decades of international engagement, the causes of the Republic’s collapse, the situation under Taliban rule and what Europe should understand about Afghanistan today. Novastan: You were directly involved in establishing Afghanistan’s diplomatic representation in Spain after the fall of the first Taliban regime. How did this story begin and what exactly was your role? Do you remember who the key people were and the first contacts with the Spanish authorities? Hamed Wahdat Ahmadzada: It is important to mention that diplomatic relations between what were then the Kingdom of Afghanistan and the Kingdom of Spain were established in 1950. In 1968, those relations were raised to the level of non-resident embassies. At the time, Spain handled these relations through its embassy in Tehran, Iran, while Afghanistan did so through its embassy in Paris. Following the fall of the Taliban regime at the end of 2001 and the creation of Afghanistan’s interim government, many countries established diplomatic relations with the newly formed Afghan government. Initially, they did so through their representations in neighbouring countries such as Pakistan or the countries of Central Asia, and subsequently through the opening of resident diplomatic missions in Kabul. The Afghanistan pavilion at Expo Zaragoza 2008, held in the Spanish city of Zaragoza. Photo: Courtesy of Hamed Wahdat Ahmadzada. Although bilateral diplomatic relations between Spain and Afghanistan already existed, it was not until 2005 that the Embassy of the Kingdom of Spain in Afghanistan was established in Kabul. The first resident ambassador, José Turpín Molina, was appointed in March 2006. That same year, following a decision by the Afghan government, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs began the necessary procedures to establish the first Embassy of the Islamic Republic of Afghanistan in Spain. How do you create a diplomatic representation practically from scratch? Where was it initially based, what resources did you have and what difficulties did you encounter? We would be particularly interested in an anecdote or episode from those first months that helps reconstruct how this relationship was born. The creation of a diplomatic representation has two important phases. The first is the preparatory phase, when the two governments make contact and express their interest in raising diplomatic relations to the level of resident embassies in their respective capitals. It should be noted that this does not have to be reciprocal: there is no requirement for both countries to establish resident embassies at the same time. Once the approval of the receiving country has been obtained, the diplomatic and administrative structure of the representation is determined internally and the head and members of the diplomatic mission are nominated. Behind the scenes of Hamed Wahdat Ahmadzada’s television interview with Zaragoza TV, showing the studio setup and recording crew. Photo: Courtesy of Hamed Wahdat Ahmadzada. The second phase, or implementation phase, begins when the receiving country is informed of the members of the diplomatic delegation and, in accordance with the Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations, the relevant diplomatic visas are requested. Subsequently, following approval by the receiving country, the members of the diplomatic corps move to the new mission. In my case, because of my academic training at the Diplomatic School in Madrid and my knowledge of the Spanish language and the country, I was chosen to be the first resident Afghan diplomat in Spain. After obtaining the relevant diplomatic visa, I arrived in Spain in December 2006 to establish initial contacts and begin the first procedures related to setting up the Afghan embassy in Madrid. In Spain, these procedures are normally carried out with the cooperation of the Directorate-General for Protocol, Chancellery and Orders of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Cooperation. In our case, following the protocol meetings and initial contacts, we began the procedures for obtaining diplomatic accreditation, registering the premises and dealing with other administrative matters related to the embassy. The great challenge was creating a new mission literally from scratch. That included finding premises, adapting them for diplomatic representation, equipping and furnishing them and, in general, creating a functioning mission in the shortest possible time. The entire process was therefore not only complex from an official and diplomatic perspective, but also required an enormous logistical, administrative and financial effort. It meant combining bilateral diplomatic meetings with all the complexities involved in establishing and adapting premises worthy of representing a country. In this particular case, during the first few months, the weight of all these responsibilities fell on me. But it was an enormous experience and a great honour. A diplomatic meeting involving Hamed Wahdat Ahmadzada in Spain during the early years of Afghanistan’s diplomatic engagement with the country. Photo: Courtesy of Hamed Wahdat Ahmadzada. How did Spain perceive the new Afghanistan in those early years, and how did Afghanistan view Spain? From your experience, were there Spanish politicians, diplomats, journalists, development workers or other figures who played a particularly important role or understood the country especially well? From the Spanish perspective, the new Afghanistan was initially perceived as an opportunity to contribute to the reconstruction of a state that had suffered decades of war and isolation. https://www.azernews.az/region/265600.ht.body: Germany plans social media restrictions for children under 13 15 October 2026 12:34 (UTC+04:00) Qabil Ashirov Read more The German government has approved the main principles of a strategy to strengthen the protection of children and teenagers in the digital environment, including age restrictions on social media and additional online safety measures. The proposed rules would prohibit children under the age of 13 from using social media, while teenagers aged 13 to 18 would face graduated restrictions. Platforms specifically designed for children could be exempt from the measures. The government plans to introduce a reliable age-verification system through a digital identity platform from 2027. The system would allow users to confirm their age without sharing all the information contained in their identity documents. Social media platforms would then be able to verify whether users meet the applicable age requirements. The strategy also envisages the development of a unified educational programme for primary school pupils to promote safe and informed use of artificial intelligence. Awareness campaigns aimed at parents are also planned. In addition, the government intends to introduce measures for the early detection of risks associated with children's digital media use and establish an online complaints service for young users. The proposed strategy forms part of Germany's efforts to improve online child protection through age verification, digital education and stronger safeguards for younger users. Tags: Germany children social media

https://iz.ru/2184561/2026-10-15/krizis-.body: Отношения Украины и США вновь оказались подорваны после того, как работа интернет-терминалов Starlink была ограничена. Это помешало украинским беспилотникам набирать необходимую для работы скорость. Также Киев обвинил Вашингтон в прекращении обмена разведывательной информацией. Что пишут СМИ о разладе между странами — в дайджесте «Известий». Associated Press: украинские БПЛА снижают скорость из-за ограничений Starlink Украинские беспилотники несколько снизили свою скорость после внезапного введения ограничений на использование в боевых действиях коммуникационных терминалов Starlink американского производства. В то же время Киев не получил обычного предварительного предупреждения от своих западных партнеров об ударах, заявил президент Украины Владимир Зеленский . Это вызвало опасения по поводу того, что Украина лишается жизненно важной разведывательной информации, особенно со стороны США. Associated Press Зеленский не уточнил, о каких именно партнерах идет речь, когда он говорит об отсутствии предупреждения. Президент США Дональд Трамп заявил, что США не прекратили обмениваться разведывательной информацией с Украиной. Эти события вызвали недовольство украинских военных и усилили опасения по поводу ухудшения отношений Киева с Вашингтоном. Украинские чиновники обеспокоены тем, что поддержка со стороны США, особенно в отношении обмена военной разведкой и использования спутниковой системы связи Starlink Илона Маска, может оказаться под угрозой. К вечеру 14 октября операторы дронов сообщали об улучшении качества передачи данных на скоростях до 160 км/ч. Однако этого всё еще слишком мало для перехвата реактивных беспилотников, и стране необходимо снять все ограничения. Маск заявил, что военная версия Starlink контролируется американскими военными и Трампом . Ограниченное состояние: Украина пытается нарастить поддержку ЕС из-за размолвки с США Пауза в передаче разведданных и отключение Starlink грозят ВСУ потерей координации войск The Washington Post: предупреждения США сеют путаницу и тревогу на Украине Доступ Украины к сети Starlink был ограничен без предупреждения, что усиливает путаницу относительно того, начали ли США ограничивать разведывательную и военную помощь Украине. Ее вооруженные силы используют защищенную, милитаризированную версию интернет-сервиса Starlink под названием Starshield для проведения ключевых военных операций. Starlink также важен для работы подключенных к интернету беспилотных летательных аппаратов-перехватчиков, которые обычно могут развивать скорость более 290 км/ч. The Washington Post Украинские официальные лица заявили, что их военные столкнулись с ограничениями скорости. «Подтверждаю, что компания SpaceX ввела ограничения скорости на терминалах Starlink во время их движения прошлой ночью», — заявил Сергей Бескрестнов, советник президента Украины по военным технологиям. «В настоящее время ограничение распространяется на «военный пакет» StarShield и ограничивает скорость до 160 км/ч, — написал он. — Очевидно, что этот шаг не может быть случайностью и связан с текущей политической ситуацией». Ранее эти системы работали без ограничений скорости, что позволяло Украине быстро поражать сложные цели. Ограничения скорости могут создать серьезные проблемы для логистики, а также для работы дронов и других быстро движущихся беспилотных систем. Связь может быть прервана, если эти системы превысят лимит во время работы. Тревога по поводу возможного введения ограничений скорости возникла после заявлений из офиса Зеленского об отсутствии предупреждений об ударах от западных разведок. Reuters: сможет ли Европа вмешаться в кризис отношений США и Украины В то время как Украина сообщила о проблемах со спутниковыми интернет-терминалами Starlink и исчезли данные США, предупреждающие о баллистических ракетных ударах, Киев также столкнулся с суровой реальностью: его европейские союзники не могут предложить никаких готовых альтернатив. Причины трудностей сразу не были ясны, но они возникли после очередного ухудшения отношений между США и Украиной, после того как Трамп объявил о соглашении об отмене санкций в отношении российского дизельного топлива и призвал к замене Зеленского. Reuters Европейские страны выразили решительную поддержку Украине и Зеленскому. Однако проблемы с важными данными показали, что Украина и Европа сильно зависят от американских систем как для низкоорбитальной спутниковой связи — предоставляемой SpaceX через Starlink — так и для космического инфракрасного зондирования, данные которого поступают в системы раннего предупреждения. В Европе нет готовой альтернативы, которую украинские солдаты могли бы использовать для своих беспилотников, хотя европейские правительства и компании работают над долгосрочными вариантами. Акции европейского спутникового оператора Eutelsat резко выросли после новостей о трудностях Украины со Starshield, чему способствовали предположения инвесторов о том, что европейские провайдеры могут извлечь выгоду из растущего напряжения в отношениях между Вашингтоном и Киевом. Однако Кристиан Фрайхерр фон дер Ропп, независимый консультант по спутниковым технологиям, заявил, что сеть OneWeb компании Eutelsat плохо подходит для использования в военное время. Bloomberg: Зеленский бросил вызов Трампу и отдал приказ о новых атаках Зеленский отдал приказ возобновить атаки на российские нефтеперерабатывающие заводы в условиях обостряющегося конфликта с Трампом из-за ограничений на помощь США в разведывательной деятельности. Зеленский заявил, что прекращает трехдневную паузу в ударах после того, как обвинил Трампа и миллиардера Илона Маска в ограничении способности Киева защищаться от ракетных и беспилотных атак. Bloomberg [14 октября] Зеленский заявил, что чувствует себя преданным в связи со сделкой [Трампа] по дизельному топливу и ограничениями США на использование Киевом в военных целях спутниковых терминалов, предоставленных компанией SpaceX Маска. «Жаль, что мы проигрываем, мы теряем сильного партнера, таково мое мнение, — сказал Зеленский. — Больно, когда президент Трамп выбирает одну сторону, и не нашу». Украина требует от США и союзников по НАТО объяснений по поводу внезапного ограничения доступа к спутниковому интернету SpaceX для военных целей после серии ракетных и беспилотных атак на электростанции. Зеленский заявил, что ограничения на использование военной сети Starshield уже привели к потерям, поскольку украинские перехватчики, использующие эту технологию, больше не могут эффективно защищаться от беспилотников. Оставайтесь на линии: к чему приведет ограничение доступа к Starlink для ВСУ Вашингтон бьет по боеспособности украинской армии Axios: ограничения в отношении Starlink вызывают подозрения в ответных мерах со стороны Маска и Трампа Разногласия между Трампом и Зеленским по поводу заключенной на прошлой неделе сделки по дизельному топливу углубились после того, как принадлежащая Маску спутниковая система Starlink неожиданно ограничила свою работу. Связь была частично восстановлена, но украинские власти всё еще пытаются выяснить, почему скорость соединения была снижена и кто за это ответственен. Axios Высокопоставленный американский чиновник заявил, что администрация Трампа не имеет никакого отношения к предполагаемым ограничениям работы сервиса Starlink. Однако украинские чиновники по-прежнему относятся к этому с подозрением. По их словам, система отключалась, когда скорость дрона превышала 160 км/ч. В некоторых случаях она отключалась, когда скорость превышала 80 км/ч. Министерство обороны Украины заявило, что SpaceX продолжает ограничивать скорость Starlink до 160 км/ч — это значительно выше, чем раньше, но всё еще намного ниже нормальной скорости. Ведомство заявило, что продолжает поддерживать связь «с партнерами и компанией SpaceX относительно стабильных условий обслуживания и предотвращения внезапных ограничений». Поделиться:

https://daryo.uz/en/2026/10/15/uzbekista.body: Uzbekistan Uzbekistan’s president signs law toughening penalties for violence against children Uzbekistan has introduced tougher penalties for crimes against children, including life imprisonment for sexual violence against children under 14 and the removal of statutes of limitations for such serious crimes, under a law signed by President Shavkat Mirziyoyev. Today, 11:00 1 min read 1 200 views 0 comments 0 Source: cpdonline.co.uk Uzbekistan has toughened penalties for crimes against children, including introducing life imprisonment for sexual violence against children under 14, under a law signed by President Shavkat Mirziyoyev. The amendments affect five codes and six laws, Saida Mirziyoyeva, head of the Presidential Administration, reported . Under the new law, perpetrators of sexual violence against children under 14 face up to 25 years in prison or life imprisonment. The statute of limitations will not apply to such serious crimes. The legislation also strengthens accountability for those who inflict physical or psychological harm on children, including employees of educational institutions and close relatives. “ “The punishment for crimes that caused the death of a child will never be mitigated,” Mirziyoyeva wrote. She added that children’s safety must not depend on circumstances and that anyone who threatens their lives, health or dignity must face strict punishment. The bill was developed at the initiative of the Adolat Social Democratic Party faction on September 27 to improve the protection of children from all forms of violence. The Legislative Chamber adopted the bill in its first reading on September 29 and in its second reading on September 30. The Senate approved the legislation on October 2, paving the way for its signing by the president. # children # crimes # penalties # reforms # rights # violence # violenceprevention Telegram channel @daryo_eng Subscribe What do you think? https://24.kg/en/article/parliament-of-k.body: The Parliament of Kyrgyzstan approved amendments to the Labor Code in the third reading on October 15, providing for wage indexation in response to rising consumer prices for goods and services. The bill was initiated by a group of MPs. The proposed amendments aim to establish wage indexation in law and introduce a unified legal framework for its implementation, regardless of an organization’s form of ownership. According to the explanatory note, the current Labor Code guarantees employees the right to fair remuneration but does not establish a clear mechanism for preserving the real value of wages. Following the adoption of a new Labor Code in 2025, the provision in the previous code requiring mandatory wage indexation ceased to apply. The amendments propose supplementing Article 91 of the Labor Code with a provision stipulating that the real value of wages will be maintained through indexation in line with rising consumer prices for goods and services. Indexation procedures for organizations funded from the state budget will be determined by Kyrgyzstan’s regulatory legal acts. Other organizations will be able to establish their procedures through collective agreements, accords or internal regulations. The explanatory note cites inflation and the rising cost of living as the reasons for the proposed amendments.

https://24.kg/en/article/zhapykeev-suvan.body: Former head of the Service for Combating Economic Crimes Syimyk Zhapykeev and former Interior Minister Omurbek Suvanaliev have failed the Kyrgyz language examination required to run in the presidential election. They told BBC about the results. Both took the test at the state institution Kyrgyztest on October 8. Omurbek Suvanaliev acknowledged that his lack of experience in written work had affected his results. He said he received a low score in that section. "I prepared for about 20 days. In fact, I have little experience with writing. I worked as a manager for 40 years: managers usually listen and give instructions, but do not do much writing themselves. I also did very little typing on a computer. That is why the written section was more difficult for me. I regret that I could not reach B2 level,” Suvanaliev told BBC. He added that he would consider retaking the examination. Syimyk Zhapykeev said he disagreed with the test results. He noted that he had studied at a Kyrgyz-language school and in a Kyrgyz-language university group, and that he was able to hold a full conversation in Kyrgyz. The former head of the Service for Combating Economic Crimes said the questions were too difficult and expressed doubts about the results of the written section, which candidates completed on a computer. « I failed at the very first hurdle. I worked in the prosecutor’s office for many years and investigated most cases in Kyrgyz. But I failed, just like General Suvanaliev. Syimyk Zhapykeev Earlier, journalist Aslan Sartbaev published the results of both candidates on Facebook. According to his post, Suvanaliev scored 87 points in reading, 84 in listening, 56 in writing and 65 in speaking. Zhapykeev scored 63 in reading, 76 in listening, 55 in writing and 63 in speaking. Presidential elections in Kyrgyzstan are scheduled for January 27, 2027. Incumbent President Sadyr Japarov intends to run. On Wednesday, entrepreneur Aimen Kasenov submitted an application to the Central Election Commission to nominate himself as an independent candidate. He also took part in the 2020–2021 presidential election. The candidate nomination period will remain open until November 13, 2026.

https://www.azernews.az/analysis/265497..body: Armenia’s referendum dilemma exposes contradictions in Pashinyan’s peace agenda 14 October 2026 20:17 (UTC+04:00) Elnur Enveroglu Read more Although 2026 is already approaching its last two months, the signing of a final peace treaty between Azerbaijan and Armenia still appears to be a distant prospect. In a recent statement to the press, Armenia’s prime minister, Nikol Pashinyan, said that "holding a referendum in the country was unrealistic", while also addressing several other important issues. He first spoke about the need to regulate relations between Yerevan and Moscow, before stressing the importance of implementing a range of reforms to meet the European Union’s requirements. It is worth recalling that, at the beginning of this year, Armenian officials repeatedly stressed during speeches in parliament that a referendum was essential in the context of preparations for EU membership. In an interview with a local television channel in February 2025, Pashinyan even referred to Azerbaijan, describing a referendum as an important and integral element of the peace agenda. Although this statement provoked considerable anger and pressure against the Yerevan administration, the course pursued by Armenia had, by the end of this year, raised hopes among many that a referendum would take place. However, the current situation and Pashinyan’s new vision once again expose contradictory positions on the peace agenda. The Armenian prime minister says that all outstanding issues relating to peace have been resolved, yet he describes holding a referendum as unrealistic. Why, then, is Armenia relegating its peace agenda with Azerbaijan to the background, while seeking, for the time being, to put the referendum question aside as it attempts to strike a balance between Europe and Russia? Armenia has long made efforts to integrate with the European Union and has been considering how to loosen its economic ties with Russia without causing a major economic crisis. Last week, after attending the summit of Commonwealth of Independent States countries in Turkmenistan, Pashinyan may have gained a deeper understanding, following his contacts with Russia, of just how heavily his country remains tied to Russian economic networks and how far-reaching the changes would need to be to break free of them. Consider that 98% of Armenia’s agricultural sector, 87% of its natural gas supply and 70% of its electricity supply are linked to Russia. These figures suggest that, for geographical and historical reasons alike, Armenia will have to undertake much more substantial reforms over a prolonged period if it is to overcome this dependence. Otherwise, its inability to disengage from Russia in the near future could slow its European ambitions and lead to further delays in holding a referendum. A referendum on constitutional changes could also expose Pashinyan to additional political risks. The prime minister would not automatically lose his position if a constitutional referendum failed, but analysts and European institutions view such an outcome as a potentially severe political blow that could derail his broader political agenda. More specifically, if the public rejected the new constitution, the peace process with Azerbaijan could stall or collapse, risking renewed regional instability, as critics have warned. Such an outcome would weaken Pashinyan’s domestic legitimacy and embolden pro-Russian opposition factions in parliament. The conclusion, therefore, is that the Armenian government does not want to put its future at risk by embarking on an economic and political gamble while reforms remain incomplete. Significant commitments to Azerbaijan, Russia and Europe are at stake. Although Armenia may look to Europe to help meet its security needs and other requirements, it must still confront some difficult realities. Above all, while seeking to preserve regional stability, Armenia remains compelled to find common ground with Moscow to maintain its economic and security ties with Russia. https://www.azernews.az/nation/265558.ht.body: Azerbaijan accuses Iranian TV channel of falsely presenting Türkiye footage as hijab rally in Baku 14 October 2026 15:43 (UTC+04:00) Akbar Novruz Read more Azerbaijan's Media and Broadcasting Council has accused Iran's Sahar Azeri television channel of spreading disinformation by presenting footage from an event in Türkiye as a rally held in Azerbaijan in support of women wearing the hijab. According to a statement issued by the Council, the channel used footage recorded in Türkiye's Diyarbakır province and falsely attributed the event to Azerbaijan. The Council described the misrepresentation of the event's location and nature as a gross falsification of facts and a deliberate attempt to manipulate public opinion. "The channel's activities are characterized by the dissemination of biased, factually incorrect information directed against Azerbaijan and the misleading of public opinion through provocative content. The channel's systematic distortion of events concerning our country, its regular airing of disinformation, and its approach aimed at shaping a negative image of Azerbaijan demonstrate that such activity is a core component of its information policy. It is precisely because of this consistent and biased conduct that the channel has been blacklisted," the statement said. The Council stated that the Iranian broadcaster had repeatedly distorted events concerning Azerbaijan and disseminated misleading information aimed at creating a negative perception of the country. It also confirmed that the television channel had been placed on a blacklist because of what it described as systematic and biased reporting. The Media and Broadcasting Council called on media organisations to ensure accuracy and objectivity when reporting information and to avoid presenting material in ways that distort events or manipulate public opinion. The Council also urged the public to critically assess information circulating in the media and on social platforms, verify claims through reliable sources and refrain from contributing to the spread of disinformation. https://en.kabar.kg/news/kyrgyz-parliame.body: www Bishkek, Oct. 15, 2026. /Kabar/. Members of the Jogorku Kenesh (Parliament of Kyrgyzstan) have adopted, in three readings, bills to ratify agreements on the abolition of visas for short-term travel with the Seychelles, and on mutual visa exemptions for holders of certain types of passports with the Togolese Republic. Under the agreement with the Seychelles, citizens of both countries may stay in the territory of the other without a visa for up to 30 days per visit, provided that the total duration of stays does not exceed 90 days within a calendar year. The agreement with Togo provides for visa exemptions for holders of diplomatic and service passports from Kyrgyzstan, as well as diplomatic and official passports from Togo. The permitted duration of stay is up to 90 days within any 180-day period. Furthermore, the deputies adopted, in the first reading, a bill to ratify an agreement between Kyrgyzstan and Togo on the promotion and reciprocal protection of investments. The document establishes international legal guarantees for the protection of investors' rights when conducting business activities within the territories of both countries. Print

Geographically situated at the intersection of Asia and Europe, Azerbaijan plays an increasingly important role as a connecting hub in the Eurasian space, President Ilham Aliyev said in his speech at the 7th CICA Summit. The head of state noted: “Our country’s cooperation with many states in bilateral and multilateral formats across the political, economic, transport, energy and humanitarian fields, in turn, strengthens the security system in our region.” The 7th Summit of the Conference on Interaction and Confidence-Building Measures in Asia (CICA) is taking place in Baku under Azerbaijan’s chairmanship. The summit will review the progress made in the CICA transformation process, which began in 2022, as well as the results of Azerbaijan’s chairmanship in strengthening the organization and promoting practical cooperation among member states. The summit is attended by heads of state and government, as well as delegations from CICA member states, observer states, observer organizations, and partner entities. The summit presents an important opportunity to discuss issues of dialogue and confidence-building among member states in a complex international environment characterized by intensifying interstate tensions, escalating conflicts, and the emergence of new hotspots of tension, including in Asia. One of the summit’s most significant outcomes is considered to be the admission of Laos into the CICA as a new member. The event will also be marked by the adoption of documents aimed at intensifying activities within the CICA and improving cooperation in specific areas. The Baku Declaration is expected to be the summit’s main political document. In it, Azerbaijan’s chairmanship of the CICA will receive the approval of all member states, and the initiatives put forward and activities carried out over the past two years in various areas will be welcomed. The document will also contain specific provisions regarding the strengthening of the international order and ways to counter risks in the military-political, economic, environmental, and other spheres. The Baku Declaration will place special emphasis on promoting tolerance and intercultural dialogue, advancing the use of science, education, and innovation in the interests of security and well-being, as well as the opportunities and risks associated with the development of artificial intelligence. In addition to the Baku Declaration, the summit also plans to adopt a separate statement on occupational safety and health. https://www.amnesty.org/ru/latest/news/2.body: • Убийства мирных жителей в ходе совместных боевых операций • Гибель мирных жителей от пыток в местах содержания под стражей: задержанных избивали, пытали электрическим током и имитацией утопления • Целенаправленные нападения на представителей народа фулани, арабов и туарегов Новый доклад Amnesty International посвящён совместным операциям военнослужащих Вооружённых сил Мали и сотрудников ЧВК «Вагнер», в ходе которых в период с 2023 по 2025 год совершались военные преступления, в том числе убийства и пытки мирных жителей. В докладе «Не щадят никого»: военные преступления, совершённые армией Мали и их иностранными союзниками у границы с Мавританией» зафиксированы как минимум 34 случая убийств мирных жителей в семи населённых пунктах Мали в период с июня 2023 года по декабрь 2025 года, совершённые малийской армией (FAM – Forces armées maliennes) и ЧВК «Вагнер» (российской частной военной компанией, действовавшей в Мали с конца 2021 по июнь 2025 года). В докладе также зафиксированы другие серьёзные нарушения международного гуманитарного права и международного права в области прав человека, такие как пытки, насильственные исчезновения, а также грабежи и уничтожение имущества гражданского населения. «Результаты нашего расследования свидетельствуют о страшной судьбе мирных жителей, оказавшихся в зоне конфликта и заплативших за это самую высокую цену, при том, что предполагаемые виновные пользуются полной безнаказанностью. Власти Мали не могут отклонить эти крайне серьёзные обвинения, не проведя беспристрастного и эффективного расследования предполагаемых преступлений», – заявил Марсо Сивьед, региональный директор Amnesty International в Западной и Центральной Африке. «Власти Мали должны обеспечить защиту гражданскому населению во время проведения военных операций, соблюдать нормы международного гуманитарного права и следить за их соблюдением, как можно скорее объяснить структуру управления иностранными боевыми частями, действующими на территории страны, а также осуществлять контроль за их действиями с помощью независимого внутреннего механизма привлечения к ответственности», – добавил он. Незаконные убийства мирных жителей В докладе подробно описаны семь инцидентов, в ходе которых в регионах Сегу, Мопти и Тимбукту были незаконно убиты 34 человека. Согласно информации, собранной Amnesty International, ни один из погибших на момент смерти не принимал непосредственного участия в боевых действиях. Они были преднамеренно застрелены во время попыток бегства или после арестов. Кому-то перерезали горло, других сожгли заживо или уже после смерти. Двенадцатого февраля 2025 года в Тин-Аданда, небольшом поселении в регионе Тимбукту, в ходе совместного патрулирования армейских частей и ЧВК «Вагнер» были убиты четыре человека. Хана*, женщина, которая выжила и нашла убежище в Мберре (Мавритания), потеряла там двух сыновей и двоюродного брата, которых сначала задержали, а затем убили. Описывая участников военной операции, она сказала: «В основном это были белые мужчины, которых сопровождали военнослужащие армии Мали». Удары беспилотников по гражданскому населению В докладе подробно описаны два удара беспилотников, нанесённых армией Мали по рынку в Эждеире (16 марта 2025) и по частному дому в Тангате (ноябрь 2025) в регионе Тимбукту, в результате которых погибли в общей сложности не менее 23 человек, в том числе как минимум пять детей. «Мы не обнаружили никаких признаков присутствия членов вооружённых группировок или военных целей ни на одном из мест ударов беспилотников. Если информация подтвердится, то эти удары будут считаться прямыми нападениями на гражданское население и гражданские объекты и должны быть расследованы как возможные военные преступления», – отметил Марсо Сивьед. В Эждеире удар беспилотника был нанесён в дневное время без предупреждения по многолюдному рынку. Семнадцатого марта 2025 года малийские военные заявили, что нанесли удар по «скоплениям террористов» в транзитном лагере в 109 км к северо-западу от Лере, убив «11 террористов». Согласно анализу, проведённому Amnesty, предоставленная армией Мали информация, прежде всего данные о месте, соответствуют удару беспилотника в Эждеире. Даже если бы там находились боевики или военные цели, нанесение удара по рынку в момент, когда там находились мирные жители, и таким образом, что это привело к жертвам среди гражданского населения, будет считаться неизбирательным. Неизбирательные нападения, в результате которых гибнут и получают ранения мирные жители, являются военными преступлениями, если они совершаются умышленно или по неосторожности. По словам семи человек, некоторые из которых потеряли родных или сами получили ранения в результате удара по рынку в Эждеир, опрошенных Amnesty International, а также по данным организаций гражданского общества, на рынке не было членов вооружённых формирований; все 16 погибших и семеро раненых были мирными жителями. «Нас привязали за руки к столбам; наши ноги не касались земли» Amnesty International взяла интервью у 15 мужчин из регионов Сегу, Мопти и Тимбукту, переживших пытки и другие виды жестокого обращения, которые заявили, что подвергались пыткам во время совместных патрулей армии и ЧВК «Вагнер» или во время заключения на военных базах в Лере и Нампале. Их слова также подтвердили другие, которые видели, как в ходе патрулирования или на территории этих двух военных баз пытали 30 человек. Свидетели рассказали, что пять человек, содержавшихся под стражей на базах, погибли в результате пыток и плохих условий содержания. Как показало расследование Amnesty International, эти преступления в основном совершались сотрудниками «Вагнера» в присутствии военнослужащих армии Мали, которые иногда выполняли роль переводчиков, просто стояли рядом и никак не вмешивались, а в некоторых случаях даже угрожали задержанным. Пострадавших подвешивали за руки к железной перекладине, душили, имитируя утопление, избивали железными прутьями и палками или били электрическим током. Задержанные и подвергшиеся пыткам в военных лагерях так и не предстали перед судом. Во время содержания под стражей, которое продолжалось от одного дня до четырёх месяцев, у них не было доступа ни к адвокату, ни к своим семьям. Целенаправленные нападения на фулани, арабов и туарегов Пастух из региона Сегу, сейчас беженец в Мавритании, сказал: «Они считают [солдаты и бойцы ЧВК «Вагнер»] всех пастухов террористами, поэтому они без колебаний сжигают людей и имущество. Не щадят ни слепых, ни стариков». Подавляющее большинство пострадавших от таких нарушений принадлежали к скотоводческим общинам (фулани, арабы и туареги), которых подозревали в сговоре с негосударственными вооружёнными группировками исключительно на основании их этнической принадлежности и присутствия в районе, где эти вооружённые группировки действовали. «Мы настоятельно призываем власти Мали обеспечить, чтобы виновные в военных преступлениях, совершённых в отношении представителей всех общин, понесли полную ответственность. Власти Мали должны провести расследование военных преступлений, совершенных малийскими военными, их иностранными военными партнёрами и членами вооружённых групп, подозреваемыми в совершении таких преступлений, и привлечь их к ответственности в рамках судебных разбирательств, отвечающего нормам справедливого судебного разбирательства, без применения смертной казни», – заявил Марсо Сивьед. «Гражданское население в затронутых конфликтом регионах Мали по-прежнему подвергается серьёзной опасности. Власти обязаны обеспечить его защиту и обнародовать соглашение, заключённое между правительством Мали и «Африканским корпусом», который в июне 2025 года сменил ЧВК «Вагнер» и в настоящее время осуществляет свою деятельность в Мали. Африканский союз должен осудить нарушения международного гуманитарного права в Мали и поддержать борьбу с безнаказанностью за преступления по международному праву», – подчеркнул он. Справочная информация Настоящий доклад опирается на результаты исследования, проведённого в 2025–2026 годах в десяти населённых пунктах регио

Комментируя сообщения о том, что находящийся в заключении азербайджанский исследователь и пацифист Бахруз Самедов нанёс себе порезы во время заседания Верховного суда 25 сентября, исследовательница Amnesty International по Южному Кавказу Наталья Нозадзе заявила: «Пока Бахруз Самедов остаётся в заключении, власти Азербайджана обязаны обеспечивать его право на здоровье. Ему по-прежнему не предоставляют необходимую медицинскую помощь, в том числе психологическую, а состояние его здоровья ухудшается. Отказ в медицинской помощи и ограничения на общение с семьёй могут представлять собой жестокое, бесчеловечное или унижающее достоинство обращение в нарушение международных обязательств Азербайджана в области прав человека». «Бахруз Самедов вообще не должен был оказаться в заключении. Он отбывает 15-летний срок по сфабрикованному обвинению в „государственной измене“, связанному с его мирной общественной деятельностью, журналистской работой и выступлениями за диалог с Арменией. Власти Азербайджана должны немедленно и безоговорочно освободить его». Справка По словам адвоката Зибейды Садыговой, 25 сентября во время перерыва в заседании Верховного суда Бахруз Самедов несколько раз порезал правую руку острым предметом. Азербайджанский исследователь, борец за мир и бывший автор издания OC Media Бахруз Самедов был задержан в Баку 21 августа 2024 года. Его обвинили в «государственной измене» из-за контактов с гражданами Армении, связанных с его деятельностью по вопросам урегулирования последствий конфликта и установления мира. Двадцать третьего июня 2025 года по итогам несправедливого судебного разбирательства его приговорили к 15 годам лишения свободы. Amnesty International считает обвинения против него сфабрикованными и неоднократно призывала к его немедленному и безоговорочному освобождению.

https://www.rferl.org/a/russia-ballistic.body: News Russian Missile Strikes Kill 3 In Kyiv, Knock Out Power As Zelenskyy Says West Gave No Warning By RFE/RL's Ukrainian Service October 14, 2026 07:54 CET Updated October 14, 2026 10:40 CET Russian Missile Strikes Kill 3 In Kyiv, Knock Out Power As Zelenskyy Says West Gave No Warning Share Copy link Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Email Share Share Copy link Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Email Share Prefer us on Google Ukrainian firefighters work at the site of an apartment building damaged by a Russian missile strike late on October 13 KYIV -- Moscow launched a wave of ballistic missile attacks on Kyiv overnight and into the morning, killing at least three people and injuring more than 20 others, as President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Ukraine had once again received no advance warning from its Western partners about the launches. Russian forces struck several energy facilities in Kyiv, Mayor Vitali Klitschko reported on October 14, after Ukraine accused Russia of violating a cease-fire announced by US President Donald Trump on strikes targeting energy infrastructure. At least five districts of Kyiv were plunged into emergency power outages after a Russian overnight strike hit one of the capital's main power plants, energy company DTEK reported . In a post on X on October 14, Zelenskyy said that Russia had used 39 ballistic missiles and more than 120 attack drones in overnight strikes, adding that at least 600,000 people were now without power. He warned that the outages could become even more widespread. Ukraine's Emergency Service said that three people were killed and 21 others, including one child, were injured, as rescue operations continued in Kyiv. "I never thought I would leave the country, but I have a teenage child, and for the sake of my daughter, my dog, and our safety, I will leave in the near future," a Kyiv resident told RFE/RL at the scene of the strike on a residential building. Embed share Survivors Rescued From Kyiv Building After Deadly Russian Strike by RFE/RL Embed share The code has been copied to your clipboard. width px height px The URL has been copied to your clipboard No media source currently available 0:00 0:01:42 0:00 "According to our intelligence, Russia is preparing additional ballistic missile strikes," Zelenskyy wrote late on October 13. "It is important that the world does not remain silent about this," he said, adding that "it is important that the United States really see what is happening and who is responsible for this war continuing." Zelenskyy reaffirmed Ukraine's support for an energy cease-fire. "Russia is attacking Ukraine's energy grid, residential buildings, and critical infrastructure, causing blackouts in Kyiv, disrupting water supplies, and, most tragically, killing more civilians," Denys Sienik, charge d'affaires at the Ukrainian Embassy in Washington, said following the overnight strikes. Responding to Zelenskyy's remarks that Ukraine received no advance warning of the ballistic missile launches and detected the first wave only as it approached Kyiv, the EU's ambassador to Ukraine, Katarina Mathernova wrote in a post on X that "missing warning means missing time. Time to wake a child. To get downstairs. To reach a shelter." "Ukraine needs air defense, interceptors and reliable early warnings. Every minute of warning can give someone a chance to survive," she added. The attack came days after Trump announced a deal allowing Russian diesel exports, following a conversation with Russian President Vladimir Putin on October 9. SEE ALSO: Trump Says Ukraine Should 'Get A New President' As Russia Kills At Least 20 In Air Strikes Trump has said that, under the deal, the United States would immediately import 300,000 metric tons of Russian diesel, with millions more expected to follow. The move has sparked criticism from European allies and from Democrats and Republicans, who warned that it could embolden Putin to continue his war against Ukraine. In a letter to Trump , a bipartisan group of 12 senators urged him to withdraw from the diesel deal with Putin, calling it "a gift to our adversary" and "a betrayal of our Allies." "Granting Moscow the ability to sell Russian diesel freely in global markets damages American security interests and is a betrayal of the people of Ukraine," the senators wrote in the letter. Meanwhile, former Ukrainian President Viktor Yushchenko addressed an open letter to Trump criticizing his deal with Putin on diesel fuel. "When there is talk of 'concessions' or deals with Putin, the Kremlin's answer is more missiles, more drones, and more bloodshed. Ukrainian families pay the price," he wrote. "One does not negotiate with tyrants -- one stops them," he added. https://www.rferl.org/a/ukraine-winter-r.body: Ukraine The Coming Cruel Winter: Ukrainians Brace For The Worst Amid Russia's Escalating Air Campaign By Oksana Kryvitska , Borys Sachalko and Daryna Kolomiyets October 14, 2026 11:33 CET The Coming Cruel Winter: Ukrainians Brace For The Worst Amid Russia's Escalating Air Campaign Share Copy link Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Email Share Share Copy link Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Email Share Prefer us on Google A Russian jet-powered drone strikes a bridge spanning the Dnieper River in Kyiv on October 2. KYIV -- Some are stockpiling firewood and candles. Others are buying country homes to escape from a city under bombardment. Buildings are racing to install extra power sources. Portable generators are selling briskly. Officials are considering pontoon bridges across the Dnieper River. Even a tunnel underneath. Russia's aerial campaign to pummel Ukraine into submission is increasing in intensity and ferocity; on October 14, much of Kyiv plunged into darkness as Moscow launched missiles and drones at the Ukrainian capital for a second straight night. Now, Ukrainians are bracing for what many fear could be the worst winter since the start of the full-scale invasion in February 2022. On the front lines, Ukraine’s dogged fight has ground Russian forces to a virtual standstill; in recent months, Kyiv's forces pulled off a surprising counteroffensive that has resulted in a major, albeit localized, shift on the battlefield. Embed share Russia’s Jet-Powered Shahed Drones Pose New Threat To Ukraine by RFE/RL Embed share The code has been copied to your clipboard. width px height px The URL has been copied to your clipboard No media source currently available 0:00 0:03:33 0:00 But its ability to fend off legions of jet-powered drones , cruise and ballistic missiles, and even slower propeller-driven drones, is increasingly stretched thin with the sheer number of Russian weapons ripping through the air -- and into Ukrainian buildings and bridges . And the biggest single source of weaponry for Ukraine, the United States, has slowed many of its deliveries -- most crucially, interceptors for the Patriot missile system. “The realistic scenario is that we could see a repeat of last winter. That means strikes on heat and utility infrastructure,” Oleh Popenko, who heads the Union of Utility Services Consumers of Ukraine, told Current Time . “We are absolutely not protected against this, and no one is.” A man removes snow from a restaurant terrace in Kyiv in January. Basement Bomb Shelter Ukrainians officials have struggled to respond to the loss of US interceptor missiles; European allies have supplied some, but not in adequate numbers, officials say. The US-built system is the only proven defense against high-speed hypersonic and ballistic missiles. US stockpiles have dropped to dangerously low levels as many of those interceptors were diverted to the Middle East to defend against Iranian attacks in the war that began in late February. Officials in Kyiv also fear the loss of advance intelligence: warnings of Russian missile launches, something provided largely by the Americans. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said on October 13 that, for a second night in a row, Kyiv had not received any warning from Western allies. “It's not a question: Will they be targeting data centers or gas stations? They will be targeting everything.” Adding to Kyiv’s worries: US President Donald Trump’s announcement last week of an “energy cease-fire” between Russia and Ukraine, which caught Kyiv off guard and which Zelenskyy says Russia has violated repeatedly. Trump, whose approval ratings have plummeted amid soaring diesel and gasoline prices, demanded that Ukraine stop attacking Russian refineries and said the US would be importing Russian diesel fuel. Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko and Zelenskyy’s government have traded blame over the pace of preparations in Kyiv and the surrounding region for the winter. Average Ukrainians, meanwhile, are doing what they can to prepare. Vitaliy Kupchak, who heads a condominium association for an apartment building in Kyiv’s Solomyanskiy district, said the association had levied an extra charge on residents and used the funds to build a small shelter in a basement space that used to be a “dump.” “Within about a month, everything was cleaned out, the walls and floor were painted, and people contributed whatever they could. Someone gave a sofa, someone gave a little bed,” he told RFE/RL’s Ukrainian Service during a recent tour. “When there are air raid alerts, people sometimes spend the night here. As you can see, there aren't many sleeping places, so people bring their own mats and sleeping bags and can simply lay them out on the floor here and sleep.” Damage from a Russian strike on the Northern Bridge in Kyiv on October 4 In recent weeks, Russia has launched multiple attacks on bridges spanning the Dnieper, which splits the Ukrainian capital. The city’s main government buildings, and much of the city’s population, are on the west bank, but the east bank is home to a sizable number of residents as well: about 40 percent of the urban population. Lyudmyla Petrovna, who lives in a high-rise apartment on the east bank of the Dnieper, recalled how she struggled to get through last year’s Russian barrages -- and the heating outages. She had already stashed away 5-liter bottles of drinking water in her hallways, and she had gotten an alcohol burner for her electric stove, in case the power is cut. She had packets of instant soup stacked up in cardboard boxes. “Here's a hand warmer. Socks. A power bank,” she told Current Time during a recent visit to her home, giving only her first name and patronymic. A power generator outside a central Kyiv restaurant during blackout hours (file photo) She was praying for a warmer winter, she said, citing Ukrainian village folklore that says if onions this season have no skin, the weather should not be so harsh. A growing number of Kyiv residents are snapping up country homes outside the city, if they can afford it, hoping to hunker down and avoid the worst of any coming Russian onslaught. Olena, who asked to be identified only by her first name, recently bought a house with a garden about 100 kilometers south of Kyiv. She doesn’t have to commute, which makes the transition easier. She said the main rooms have individual gas heaters, so she won’t be reliant on municipal heat. "The first thing we did was put in firewood. Oak. 3,500 hryvnyas ($78) per cubic meter ($80 per square foot), and we bought six [cubic meters] in total," she said. Others don't want to leave -- or have little choice. “There’s simply nowhere to go, that’s all. So, I’m not planning on it,” one man told RFE/RL’s Ukrainian Service. “I suppose if I had a place to go, I’d plan for it, but as it stands -- no.” Bridge To Spring Earlier this month, Russian drone strikes hit Kyiv’s Southern and Northern bridges, prompting authorities to shut or restrict traffic on those and other spans. The measures sparked major jams, tangling public transit and snarling travel citywide. Some residents resorted to crossing on foot. Government officials are now discussing preparing temporary pontoon bridges in case the existing spans are damaged beyond short-term repair. That temporary fix is even more challenging given that the Dnieper can freeze over in cold winters. Mykola Kalashnyk, the national transport minister, also said that a tunnel under the Dnieper was also under consideration. Workers at a Ukrainian thermal power plant hit by a Russian strike in Novermber 2024 Like many cities that expanded quickly during the Soviet era, much of Kyiv’s heating infrastructure is centralized in massive boiler plants that heat thousands of homes. Ukrainian authorities have raced to decentralize that system, building smaller boilers, but experts say the move is behind schedule. https://www.rferl.org/a/afghanistan-chin.body: Afghanistan 'We'll Keep Waiting': Afghanistan's Dead-End Road To China October 13, 2026 19:21 CET By Amos Chapple Photo: RFE/RL Graphics Afghanistan 'We'll Keep Waiting': Afghanistan's Dead-End Road To China October 13, 2026 19:21 CET By Amos Chapple 'We'll Keep Waiting': Afghanistan's Dead-End Road To China Share Copy link Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Email Share Share Copy link Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Email Share Prefer us on Google At the October 4 inauguration of a road built to Afghanistan’s border with China, Taliban officials faced a frosty reception from their eastern neighbor. Beijing did not send representatives or officially acknowledge the event and China’s militarized boundary remained firmly shut. Images from the inauguration showed Chinese security cameras watching from behind swaths of razor wire. A satellite image taken on October 11 confirmed Taliban claims that the new road has been built to within a few dozen meters of the Chinese border, but Zhu Yongbiao , the director of the Center for Afghanistan Studies at China’s Lanzhou University told RFE/RL that the chances of Beijing opening the mountain pass any time soon “are extremely low.” A satellite image captured on October 11 showing the new Afghan road (straight line on left) that runs to within a few dozen meters of the Chinese border. A border fence running north to south is fortified on the Chinese side with razor wire, machine-gun posts and trenches. “Afghanistan's economy is very small and its value to China is negligible,” Zhu said. “Meanwhile, the financial costs and security risks associated with opening the route would be substantial.” The Central Asian country's main exports to China are pine nuts, dried apricots, and gemstones. Zhu says Beijing views the threat of Islamist terrorism from Afghanistan as far outweighing any potential benefits to opening the border. He pointed specifically to the East Turkestan Islamic Movement (ETIM), a militant Uyghur group seeking to establish an Islamic state in China's Xinjiang region. A 2026 UN report said the group is active in Badakhshan Province, where the new road is located. Kabul “has failed to meet virtually any of China's demands concerning the handling of the ETIM," the Afghanistan expert said. "Consequently, China is unlikely to make further concessions to the Taliban in the near future." Zhu believes Afghanistan's construction of the dead-end gravel road was intended as a signal to Beijing that the Taliban is capable of developing infrastructure in the remote region. The route was reportedly built by Afghan engineers and financed by Kabul at cost of $5.6 million. At the road's inauguration, Badakhshan's Taliban-appointed governor, Rahmatullah Najib, claimed that "there are no security problems in any part" of the region. The Chinese border viewed from Afghan territory around the time of the inauguration of the road to the eastern tip of Afghanistan. Several locals in Badakhshan's Wakhan Corridor, where the road extends, described widespread hopes that a door into the world's second-largest economy will transform life in the region. “For the people of Wakhan this road represents more than a transportation project,” tour guide Yar Mohammed told RFE/RL. “It offers hope for reduced isolation, improved living conditions, and a stronger connection with the wider world.” The road completed by the Taliban is an extension of a project through the Wakhan Corridor started in 2019 under the US-backed Afghan government at the time. The construction project was abandoned amid the Taliban takeover of the country in 2021, then resumed in 2023. Mohammed says the road is already benefiting locals of the region, but added, “its real impact will depend on the official opening of the [Chinese] border.” Map: Afghanistan's "Road To Nowhere" A Taliban government report listing the reasons for pursuing a potential border crossing with China notes that "opening the Wakhan Corridor would free Afghanistan once and for all from pressure exerted by neighboring countries, which frequently use [Pakistan's] Karachi route, Gwadar Port, and [Iran's] Chabahar for political purposes, causing substantial financial losses to our traders and citizens every year." Infrastructure on the Chinese side of the high-altitude border, including a road that the Taliban’s new construction apparently aimed for, was established more than a decade ago as a means to fortify China’s militarized border with Afghanistan by improving access for Beijing’s armed patrols. Chinese media has referred to the approximately 76-kilometer border with Afghanistan as a “major counterterrorism front line.” The Wakhan Corridor is a narrow finger of Afghan territory initially established in the nineteenth century as a buffer between the Russian and British empires amid the geopolitical tussle over Central Asia known as the “Great Game.” Life in the region has been marked by extreme hardship and isolation, underscored by infant mortality reported to be as high as 30 percent. A farmer in Afghanistan's Wakhan Corridor in 2021. Ihsanullah Omarkhail , a Malaysia-based China expert agreed that Afghanistan's new road “is more symbolic than a genuine means of connecting Afghan traders with Chinese markets.” Any potential border opening would represent a situation in which the “costs outweigh the opportunities,” for Beijing, he told RFE/RL. That view is backed by sharply worded Chinese media reactions to the Afghan road construction. An article published by a commentator on the popular Sohu platform on October 10 pointed to the brief window of only around three months in summer when the 4,800-meter mountain pass would be traversable by vehicles, and the threat from Islamist terrorism. “To put it bluntly, what China is waiting for is not a path, but an answer -- can the Taliban truly control their own territory? Are the terrorist training camps still operating? Has the risk of border infiltration been controlled?,” the article asked pointedly, adding, “the barbed wire will not be dismantled until these issues are resolved.” The commentator concluded that if Afghanistan is unable to meet Beijing’s expectations regarding the suppression of militants, “we'll keep waiting. China isn't in a hurry. Afghanistan is.” Sindre Langmoen and RFE/RL's Radio Azadi contributed to this report, 'We'll Keep Waiting': Afghanistan's Dead-End Road To China Share Copy link Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Email Share Share Copy link Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Email Share Follow us Facebook X (Twitter) Youtube Instagram Follow us Print Amos Chapple Amos Chapple is a New Zealand-born writer and visual journalist with a particular interest in the former U.S.S.R.
