https://24.kg/en/article/kyrgyzstan-is-b.body: Citizens of Kyrgyzstan recruited by Russia to take part in the military operation in Ukraine can be brought home if they seek assistance in advance. Foreign Minister Jeenbek Kulubaev said this in response to a lawmaker’s question at a meeting of the Zhogorku Kenesh Committee on International Affairs, Defense, Security and Migration. Earlier, MP Aibek Altynbekov said that a Kyrgyz citizen in Russia had been forced to sign documents before a court ruling was issued and taken to a training camp. However, he did not provide further details about the man. Kulubaev said the Foreign Ministry was actively working to address the issue. "If we learn that Kyrgyz citizens are being drawn into hostilities, we manage to stop the process. Sometimes they are summoned to military enlistment offices or taken straight to a pretrial detention facility, forced to sign documents and taken away. When we learn about such cases, we manage to intervene and help many migrants. However, some leave without informing anyone. We only find out after they have left, when their parents learn what happened and contact us. Citizens can file an application, after which, through our embassy in Ukraine, we try to contact them and secure their release,” he said. Jeenbek Kulubaev added that many citizens do not report such cases, and the Foreign Ministry often learns about them only after the individuals are wounded or killed. "Sometimes even their parents know nothing. Once a person has gone to war, it becomes much more difficult to bring them back. If we know which military unit they are in and where they are stationed, we make efforts to help,” he said. The foreign minister did not disclose how many Kyrgyz citizens had been brought home from the war.

https://www.azernews.az/nation/265517.ht.body: Hizb ut-Tahrir links emerge after hijab protest outside Azerbaijan’s embassy in Ankara 14 October 2026 00:53 (UTC+04:00) AzerNEWS Staff Read more Footage of a protest outside Azerbaijan’s embassy in Ankara over alleged restrictions on the hijab was first circulated by a media platform linked to the Islamist organisation Hizb ut-Tahrir, according to Azerbaijani media reports. Musavat.com investigated the platform, Köklü Değişim Medya, after it published the first footage of the demonstration on its X account, Turkustan.az reported. According to the investigation, Köklü Değişim Medya and Köklü Değişim Dergisi belong to the Turkish representation of Hizb ut-Tahrir. Hizb ut-Tahrir, whose name translates from Arabic as the “Party of Liberation”, is an international pan-Islamist and fundamentalist political organisation founded in Jerusalem in 1953 by Palestinian Islamic scholar Taqi al-Din al-Nabhani. Initially active in East Jerusalem, the organisation subsequently expanded its activities to dozens of countries, including Lebanon, Syria, Iraq, Egypt, Tunisia and Türkiye. According to publicly available sources, Hizb ut-Tahrir differs from other Islamist movements through its extensive ideological framework and its detailed vision of the political system it seeks to establish. The organisation is banned in several countries, including Egypt, Jordan, Saudi Arabia, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Russia, China and Uzbekistan. Members have been imprisoned in a number of these countries. Hizb ut-Tahrir is also officially banned in Azerbaijan. The protest outside Azerbaijan’s embassy in Ankara was held over claims of a hijab ban. The reported links between the platform that first circulated the footage and Hizb ut-Tahrir have drawn attention to the organisation behind the initial coverage of the demonstration. The available information does not establish whether Hizb ut-Tahrir organised the protest itself or had any direct involvement in arranging it. Tags: hijab Protests

The parliamentarians also expressed concern over what they described as the Turkish authorities' tolerant attitude towards provocative actions taking place outside Azerbaijan's diplomatic missions in Türkiye. The statement called on representatives of Türkiye's ruling party to demonstrate political responsibility, respect Azerbaijan's sovereignty and constitutional order, and refrain from statements or actions that could damage relations between the two countries. The transport infrastructure developed in Garabagh and East Zangezur connects residential settlements with one another and integrates them into the country’s unified economic space, President Ilham Aliyev said in a message to the participants of the 6th Azerbaijan International Restoration, Reconstruction and Development of Garabagh Exhibition – “Rebuild Garabagh.” "To date, nearly 1,500 kilometers of roads have been constructed, and the 11.7-kilometer Murovdag tunnel stands as an important example of engineering in complex mountainous terrain. As an essential part of the Zangezur corridor, the Horadiz–Aghband railway is of strategic importance for expanding Azerbaijan’s international transport and logistics links. Energy and water supply infrastructure is also being developed to serve new residential settlements and production facilities. In the region, one new reservoir has been built and five have been restored, while 13 substations and 38 hydroelectric power plants with a total capacity of 307 megawatts have been commissioned. Developing Garabagh and East Zangezur as a “green energy zone” is one of the key priorities in building this infrastructure," the message said. Meanwhile, Caspian Construction Week, covering construction, the reconstruction of Garabagh, engineering and utility systems, the plastics and polymer industry, road infrastructure and public transport, has opened in Baku. Held at the Baku Expo Center from October 14 to 16, the event features four international exhibitions, alongside a separate international exhibition dedicated to road infrastructure and public transport. Caspian Construction Week serves as a platform for companies from various industries to showcase their products and solutions, bring together sector representatives and establish professional contacts. Its scope ranges from construction materials and heating and ventilation equipment to solutions for the reconstruction of Garabagh, plastics and polymers, road infrastructure and public transport. The exhibitions provide Azerbaijani and international companies with opportunities to present their products and technologies, keep up with market developments and discuss potential partnerships. Alongside the exhibition displays, the program includes panel discussions, innovation sessions and business presentations on a range of topics. Bilateral business-to-business (B2B) and business-to-government (B2G) meetings are also planned for exhibitors and invited companies. These meetings are intended to help participants explore cooperation opportunities with one another and with relevant government bodies. Over three days, Caspian Construction Week brings together stakeholders from construction, engineering, industry, the reconstruction of Garabagh, architecture and transport. The exhibitions and business events offer participants an opportunity to showcase products and technologies, follow industry developments and establish new business connections. Azerbaijan is expected to complete the commissioning of 11 solar and wind power plants with a combined capacity of about 2 gigawatts by the end of 2027, as part of the first phase of renewable energy development, Energy Minister Parviz Shahbazov said at the third National Competition Forum organized by the State Agency for Antimonopoly and Consumer Market Control on Wednesday, Trend ’s correspondent reports from the event. He noted that 20 gigawatts’ worth of solar and wind energy projects are currently being implemented with companies from the United Arab Emirates, including Masdar; Saudi Arabia’s ACWA Power; the UK’s BP; and companies from China and other countries. The minister emphasized that local companies are also expanding their participation in the sector. Examples include SOCAR’s involvement in green energy projects and the development by local investors of four power plants with a combined capacity of 150 megawatts in Khachmaz and Nakhchivan. The expansion of production capacity in Karabakh and East Zangezur is turning the regions into new growth hubs for Azerbaijan’s non-oil and gas sector, Azerbaijani Economy Minister Mikayil Jabbarov said in a message to participants of the sixth Azerbaijan International Exhibition for Restoration, Reconstruction and Development of Karabakh (Rebuild Garabagh), Trend ’s correspondent reports from the exhibition. The minister noted that Rebuild Garabagh, held as part of Caspian Construction Week, is an important platform bringing together reconstruction efforts in the liberated territories and investment opportunities being created in the regions. He said that, under the leadership of President Ilham Aliyev, residential areas being developed in Karabakh and East Zangezur under the “smart city” and “smart village” concepts, along with new transport corridors, green energy initiatives, and social projects, reflect the state’s strategic vision for these territories. According to Jabbarov, consistent and systematic reconstruction efforts have created broad opportunities for sustainable resettlement and economic development in the regions. The minister emphasized that tax and customs exemptions, preferential loans, loan guarantees and subsidies, industrial parks equipped with ready-to-use infrastructure, and other incentives introduced to promote entrepreneurship in the liberated territories have created a favorable business environment. He noted that additional support mechanisms had also been established under decrees signed by the president. These include covering a significant portion of the costs of transporting goods to foreign markets, including new and alternative destinations, from the state budget, as well as compensating exporters for customs clearance costs. These and other measures will help exporters operating in the liberated territories strengthen their positions in domestic and international markets. Jabbarov said that the launch of new manufacturing facilities in Karabakh and East Zangezur, along with an increase in the number of residents at the Aghdam Industrial Park and the Araz Valley Economic Zone Industrial Park, demonstrates the rapid realization of the regions’ industrial potential. “These projects will not only meet domestic demand but also enable the export of competitive products and the development of new value chains,” the minister said. He added that the regions’ abundant natural resources, favorable geographical location, energy potential, transport and logistics capabilities, and tourism prospects offer extensive opportunities for investors. According to the minister, the regions have substantial geological reserves, and extraction has already begun at several deposits. Intensive projects are also being implemented in agriculture, particularly in horticulture and livestock farming. Jabbarov emphasized that the launch of the Zangezur Corridor would further enhance the regions’ transport and logistics potential. He also noted that Karabakh and East Zangezur offer additional investment opportunities in tourism thanks to their ancient history, scenic landscapes, rich cultural heritage, and therapeutic mineral water resources. The minister called on business representatives to explore the regions’ economic potential and launch new projects. “We are confident that the Rebuild Garabagh exhibition will help present the regions’ economic potential to the business community, generate new investment initiatives and partnerships, and accelerate regional development,” Jabbarov said. He thanked all partners involved in organizing the exhibition and wished participants and visitors success, productive meetings, and new opportunities for cooperation. Cooperation with Central Asian countries has increasingly included political dialogue and efforts to identify practical areas for economic engagement.
